center.newsTitle: Video debunks John Kelly's claim that Frederica Wilson took credit for FBI building funds
newBody: White House Chief of Staff John Kelly on Thursday excoriated Rep. Frederica Wilson for bragging in 2015 about securing the federal aid to build an FBI field office in South Florida.

issue: Video Debunks Kelly's Criticism of Rep. Wilson
roundup: A video of Rep. Frederica Wilson speaking at an FBI office dedication directly contradicts General Kelly's recent claims that the Congresswoman took credit for securing federal funds for the building, for which he called her an "empty barrel". She is shown praising the two slain officers for which the building is named.

left.newsTitle: All 5 Former U.S. Presidents Team Up to Raise $31 Million for Hurricane Victims
newBody: All five of the former living U.S. presidents made a rare appearance together in the name of hurricane relief Saturday night. They were even joined by current President Donald Trump — sort of.

right.newsTitle: Five ex-presidents and Trump champion unity, volunteerism at hurricane relief concert
newBody: All five living former presidents took the stage together at Saturday evening's hurricane relief charity concert in Texas, displaying a sense of unity and speaking of the importance of volunteerism and community in the face of natural disasters.

center.newsTitle: Campaign from former presidents raises $31M for disaster relief
newBody: A fundraising campaign launched by all five living former U.S. presidents has raised $31 million in donations for disaster relief so far, after a series of hurricanes tore through different parts of the country.

issue: Former U.S. Presidents Raise $31 Million for Hurricane Victims
roundup: All five former living U.S. presidents teamed up to raise $31 million for hurricane victims, appearing on stage together at a concert on Saturday evening. President Trump also made remarks via video.

left.newsTitle: Trump pledges ‘NO change to your 401(k)’ in his tax cut plan
newBody: President Trump vowed on Monday that his tax cut plan would not include any changes to tax-deferred retirement accounts such as 401(k)s, following reports last week that House Republicans were weighing a sharp reduction in the amount of income American workers could save through such programs.

right.newsTitle: Trump knocks down reports of big 401(k) squeeze in GOP tax plan: 'NO change'
newBody: President Trump on Monday adamantly denied reports that the Republican tax plan could drastically reduce the amount of pretax money Americans are allowed to contribute to their 401(k) plans, vowing “NO change” to the retirement account rules.

center.newsTitle: Trump Says ‘No Change’ to 401(k) Plans Under Forthcoming Tax Proposal
newBody: President Donald Trump on Monday morning vowed a popular retirement savings program would remain untouched in the forthcoming Republican tax overhaul proposal.

issue: ’No Change’ to 401(k) Plans
roundup: President Trump vowed on Monday that his tax cut plan would not include any changes to tax-deferred retirement accounts such as 401(k)s, following reports last week that House Republicans were weighing a sharp reduction in the amount of income American workers could save through such programs.

left.newsTitle: Exclusive: Why One of Vladimir Putin's Biggest Critics Is Banned From U.S.
newBody: A prominent critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin, who championed sanctions against his country, is being banned from entering the U.S.—but he tells Newsweek he expects a quick resolution.

right.newsTitle: ​Russia Puts Putin Critic on Wanted List; State Dept. Revokes His Visa
newBody: The State Department revoked the visa of a U.S.-born businessman and chief critic of Vladimir Putin after Russia exposed a loophole and unilaterally added him to Interpol's wanted list, The Guardian reported.

center.newsTitle: Lawmakers want immediate review of travel restriction on Putin critic
newBody: The United States government has revoked travel privileges for a fierce critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin, stirring alarm on Capitol Hill.

issue: Trump Administration Revokes Visa of Putin Critic
roundup: The Trump administration has revoked the visa of Bill Browder, a top critic of Vladimir Putin who successfully pushed Congress to impose Russian sanctions in 2012. Several senators, led by John McCain, are requesting that the decision be reviewed immediately.

left.newsTitle: Corker says White House should stay out of tax debate; Trump fires back with insult
newBody: Senator Bob Corker (R-Tenn.) admonished President Trump on Tuesday to stop interfering in the debate over tax legislation and said his volatility could lead the United States into war, prompting a slew of Twitter insults from the president and renewing a long-simmering feud just hours before he is scheduled to visit Capitol Hill.

right.newsTitle: Trump rips Corker: 'Couldn’t get elected dog catcher'
newBody: President Trump slammed Sen. Bob Corker on Tuesday for going “negative on anything Trump” after the retiring Republican lawmaker ramped up criticism of the administration and its policies.

center.newsTitle: Trump, key Republican U.S. senator spar ahead of tax meeting
newBody: A senior Republican senator called President Donald Trump “utterly untruthful” on Tuesday in an exchange of insults on Twitter hours before the president was to meet with lawmakers on Capitol Hill to build consensus for tax reform.

issue: Senator Corker Spars with Trump
roundup: Senator Bob Corker (R-TN) called President Donald Trump “utterly untruthful” on Tuesday in an exchange of insults on Twitter hours before the president was to meet with lawmakers on Capitol Hill to build consensus for tax reform.

left.newsTitle: Puerto Rico’s infrastructure will be rebuilt by a 2-person company with ties to Ryan Zinke
newBody: Puerto Rico's infrastructure is in desperate need of repair, which makes it all the more puzzling that the commonwealth's state-owned utility hired an obscure Montana firm to do the job.

right.newsTitle: No-name firm with Zinke ties lands $300M Puerto Rico power contract
newBody: A tiny Montana company from Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke’s hometown inked a $300 million contract to help restore electrical power on Puerto Rico, according to a report Tuesday.

center.newsTitle: Small company from Trump Interior chief's hometown wins massive contract to restore Puerto Rico's power
newBody: A small Montana company located in Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke's hometown has signed a $300 million contract to help get the power back on in Puerto Rico, The Washington Post reported.

issue: Small Company With Zinke Ties Wins Puerto Rico Contract
roundup: A very small company with ties to Ryan Zinke, Trump's Interior Secretary, that only had 2 employees when Hurricane Maria hit Puerto Rico has won a $300 million contract to restore power to the island.

left.newsTitle: Sen. Jeff Flake shouldn’t retire. He should run for reelection.
newBody: In retiring, Flake is letting Trump win.

right.newsTitle: This Flake got snowed — and soon will melt away
newBody: Arizona Republican Sen. Jeff Flake unburdened himself and burdened the rest of us Tuesday with what may rank as one of the worst-delivered nationally televised speeches in the history of the U.S. Senate.

center.newsTitle: Republican Senator and Trump critic says will not seek re-election
newBody: U.S. Republican Senator Jeff Flake, one of the most prominent critics of President Donald Trump, said on Tuesday he was out of step with his party and would not seek re-election.

issue: AZ Senator Jeff Flake Will Not Seek Re-election
roundup: Retiring Sen. Jeff Flake, R-Ariz., said Wednesday he decided not to run again for his Senate seat because he had no chance of winning a GOP primary race in his state with President Trump in the White House.

left.newsTitle: While you aren’t looking, the GOP continues to gut financial oversight
newBody: While Washington – and political Twitter – remain consumed by the battle of words between President Trump and Tennessee Senator Bob Corker, not to mention the latest attempts by the Republicans to move tax reform forward, an important Republican effort to weaken financial oversight and accountability is proceeding onward behind the scenes.

right.newsTitle: Mike Pence casts tie-breaking vote to cancel Obama-era rule favoring class-action suits against banks
newBody: With Vice President Mike Pence casting the deciding vote, the Senate voted late Tuesday night to undo a rule issued by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau that would bar financial firms from contracts that rule out class-action lawsuits related to their products. The measure now goes to President Trump's desk.

center.newsTitle: Republicans, Wall Street score victory in dismantling class-action rule
newBody: Banks, credit card issuers and other financial companies will be able to block customers from banding together to sue over disputes, after the U.S. Senate on Tuesday narrowly killed a rule banning the firms from using “forced arbitration” clauses.

issue: Senate Strikes Down Class-Action Lawsuit Rule
roundup: The Senate has effectively rescinded the Obama-era rule that guaranteed individuals the right to bring class-actions suits against banks and credit card companies. Many on the Left are criticizing the move, arguing it gives Wall Street more opportunity to cheat consumers, while others on the Right saw the old rule as a political gift to trial lawyers.

left.newsTitle: Trump will declare opioid epidemic a public health emergency, not a national emergency
newBody: Donald Trump has talked big about the action he was going to take to combat the opioid epidemic, describing it as a “national emergency,” which he said he was “saying officially, right now” back in August. Except he wasn't actually officially declaring a national emergency then or at any of the other times he decided to try to sound serious about opioids. The day of the official declaration has come and … Trump isn’t declaring a national emergency. Instead, he’s declaring a public health emergency.

right.newsTitle: Trump to declare opioid epidemic public health emergency – here’s what that means
newBody: President Trump is officially declaring the opioid crisis a “public health emergency.”
Trump told reporters in August that the epidemic is a “serious problem the likes of which we have never had” and had promised to declare it a national emergency.

center.newsTitle: White House: Trump to declare opioid crisis a public health emergency
newBody: President Trump on Thursday will instruct the acting director of the Department of Health and Human Services to declare the opioid epidemic a public health emergency, White House officials said.

issue: Trump To Declare Opioids a Health Emergency
roundup: President Trump is officially declaring the opioid crisis a “public health emergency.” Trump told reporters in August that the epidemic is a “serious problem the likes of which we have never had."

left.newsTitle: San Juan mayor feuds with energy firm when it threatens to stop work after audit request
newBody: A letter sent by Puerto Rico Gov. Ricardo Rossello to the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general’s office on Wednesday touched off a Twitter feud and later apology by the small Montana-based company that earned a contract to restore power on the island.

right.newsTitle: Puerto Rico, Whitefish defend controversial power contract
newBody: Puerto Rico and Whitefish Energy Holdings on Tuesday defended their $300 million contract for the small Montana company to repair the U.S. territory's hurricane-ravaged power grid after the deal was criticized by U.S. lawmakers.

center.newsTitle: Puerto Rico gov requests audit into contract awarded to tiny energy company
newBody: The governor of Puerto Rico is requesting an audit into how a small energy company from Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke’s Montana hometown won a multimillion-dollar contract to restore power to Puerto Rico.

issue: Audit Requested into $300 Million Contract
roundup: Puerto Rico Gov. Ricardo Rossello has requested a federal audit to investigate why a $300 million contract to restore the island's power was awarded to a very small company with ties to Donald Trump's Interior Secretary, Ryan Zinke.

left.newsTitle: Tax Cuts Are the Glue Holding a Fractured Republican Party Together
newBody: One week before they are set to unveil a sprawling overhaul of the federal tax code, Republicans struggled on Wednesday with key parts of their plan, reigniting a fight over retirement savings and racing to cut a deal with lawmakers from high-tax states ahead of a critical budget vote in the House on Thursday.

right.newsTitle: House passes $4 trillion budget, clears way for Trump tax plan
newBody: House Republicans on Thursday narrowly adopted the Senate’s $4 trillion budget blueprint, despite grumblings about the impact on the deficit and the elimination of state and local tax deductions.

center.newsTitle: House Republicans just cleared the way for tax reform
newBody: The House passed the Senate's budget resolution on Thursday by a vote of 216 to 212, in the last procedural step before the GOP can move to fast-track tax-reform legislation that's expected to be unveiled next week.

issue: GOP Budget Passes the House
roundup: In a narrow vote of 216-212, the House of Representatives passed the Senate's budget resolution, paving the way for the GOP's plan to reform the tax code.

left.newsTitle: JFK files reveal FBI warning on Oswald and Soviets' missile fears
newBody: The publication of nearly 3,000 previously classified files relating to the assassination of John F Kennedy in 1963 reveals that the FBI had warned Dallas police about a threat to kill Lee Harvey Oswald, and claims that Soviet officials feared an “irresponsible” US general could launch a missile strike in the wake of the crisis.

right.newsTitle: JFK Files: 'Big news' coming, British reporter was told before shots fired
newBody: A senior reporter at a British newspaper received an anonymous phone call prior to President John F. Kennedy’s assassination, alerting the reporter to “some big news” about 25 minutes in advance, according to a CIA file released Thursday.

center.newsTitle: Trump releases some JFK files, blocks others under pressure
newBody: U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday ordered the unveiling of 2,800 documents related to the 1963 assassination of President John F. Kennedy but yielded to pressure from the FBI and CIA to block the release of other records to be reviewed further.

issue: Release of Some JFK Files
roundup: U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday ordered the unveiling of 2,800 documents related to the 1963 assassination of President John F. Kennedy but sided with the FBI and CIA to block the release of other records to be reviewed further.

left.newsTitle: The shadiest details in Puerto Rico's leaked electricity contract with Whitefish Energy
newBody: Puerto Rico has now endured the longest power failure in U.S. history, after Category 4 Hurricane Maria tore a path of destruction across the island on Sept. 20. One of the contracts the island's beleaguered government signed in order to get the lights turned back on is with a tiny Montana-based company named Whitefish Energy.

right.newsTitle: Leaked Whitefish contract to restore Puerto Rico's power shows attempt to avoid government oversight
newBody: A leaked copy Whitefish’s contract to restore power in Puerto Rico, which circulated online Thursday night, reveals how the energy company and the island’s power utility sought to avoid government oversight of the deal.

center.newsTitle: Leaked document reveals Whitefish contract blocks government from reviewing costs or profits
newBody: A deal reached between the government and a small Montana energy company located in Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke's hometown prohibits the government from reviewing labor costs or profits related to the company's relief efforts in Puerto Rico, according to a leaked copy of the contract.

issue: Leaked Power Contract Shows Audit Restrictions
roundup: A leaked copy of the $300 million power contract awarded to Whitefish Energy, the very small company with ties to Donald Trump's Interior Secretary, shows that both the federal government and Puerto Rico have been barred from auditing the costs and profits associated with the job.

left.newsTitle: Robert Mueller's First Charges
newBody: The special counsel overseeing the Russia investigation reportedly obtained a sealed indictment on Friday.

right.newsTitle: Mueller probe into possible collusion with Russia nets first charges: report
newBody: Robert Mueller’s investigation into possible collusion between the Trump campaign and Russia have reportedly netted its first charges.

center.newsTitle: First charges filed in U.S. special counsel's Russia investigation: source
newBody: A federal grand jury on Friday approved the first charges in the investigation into alleged Russian meddling in the 2016 U.S. presidential election, a source briefed on the matter told Reuters.

issue: Mueller Files First Charges
roundup: Special Counsel Robert Mueller and his team have reportedly filed the first charges in the ongoing investigation into Russia's interference in the 2016 election. The indictment has been sealed by a federal judge, leaving many questions about who is involved and what the charges are.

left.newsTitle: ‘White Lives Matter’ organizers cancel second rally after taunts from counterprotesters
newBody: Crowds of protesters began gathering at 8 a.m. on a cold, cloudy Saturday. They’d come to see Nazis. But, two hours later, there were still none.

right.newsTitle: Overwhelming Presence of Tennessee Law Enforcement Ensures Peaceful ‘White Lives Matter’ Rally in Murfreesboro
newBody: The Rutherford County Sheriff’s Office, Murfreesboro Police Department, and the Tennessee State Police ensured a peaceful “White Lives Matter” rally held in this growing Nashville suburb on Saturday with an overwhelming presence that kept a white nationalist group and counter protesters completely separated.

center.newsTitle: White supremacists chant 'closed borders, white nation' in 'White Lives Matter' march
newBody: White nationalist and neo-Nazi groups took to the streets in two Tennessee towns on Saturday for so-called White Lives Matter rallies.

issue: White Supremacists Hold White Lives Matter Rally
roundup: White supremacists held a "White Lives Matter" march in Tennessee on Saturday, chanting the Nazi slogan "blood and soil" and “closed borders, white nation, now we start the deportation.” They were met by hundreds of counterprotesters, which led to the cancelation of their second rally.

left.newsTitle: Clinton campaign, DNC paid for research that led to Russia dossier
newBody: The Hillary Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee helped fund research that resulted in a now-famous dossier containing allegations about President Trump’s connections to Russia and possible coordination between his campaign and the Kremlin, people familiar with the matter said.

right.newsTitle: The Russia Dossier Story: A Perfect Storm of Clinton Deception, Media Irresponsibility, and Democratic Moral Blindness
newBody: A bombshell Washington Post story reveals Hillary’s campaign and the DNC were behind the dossier, after all.

center.newsTitle: Clinton team and Democrats 'bankrolled' Trump dirty dossier
newBody: US President Donald Trump has seized on reports that Hillary Clinton's team bankrolled a sleazy dossier of allegations linking him to Russia.

issue: Clinton and DNC Funded Trump-Russia Dossier
roundup: Hillary Clinton's campaign and the Democratic National Committee hired a Washington firm to research and create a dossier that accused Donald Trump of having multiple ties to Russia, including allegations of collusion during the election.

left.newsTitle: Puerto Rico’s power restoration efforts hit a snag as Trump-connected company gets the boot
newBody: Lawmakers call on federal government to take more active role.

right.newsTitle: FBI probes shady Puerto Rico power contract
newBody: The FBI has launched an investigation into a $300 million contract awarded to a tiny Montana electric company to ​help rebuild Puerto Rico’s power grid after the island was decimated by Hurricane Maria, it was reported on Monday.

center.newsTitle: FBI Is Probing Puerto Rico Power Contract
newBody: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating a decision by Puerto Rico’s power authority to award a $300 million contract to a tiny Montana energy firm to rebuild electrical infrastructure damaged in Hurricane Maria, according to people familiar with the matter.

issue: FBI Investigating Whitefish Energy Contract
roundup: The FBI is investigating the $300 million contract to restore Puerto Rico's power after it was awarded to a very small company with ties to Donald Trump's Interior Secretary, Ryan Zinke. The company only had 2 employees with Hurricane Marie hit.

left.newsTitle: A Day Before Presenting Their Tax Cut Plan, Republicans Still Wrestle With Key Details
newBody: House Republicans are just one day away from unveiling their long-awaited tax plan, yet many key details remain in flux.

right.newsTitle: Susan Collins doesn't back eliminating estate tax, lowering individual tax rate for wealthy
newBody: Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, does not back two key provisions in the GOP tax plan: removing the estate tax and reducing the individual tax rate for the wealthy.

center.newsTitle: Sen. Susan Collins insists on keeping taxes for the wealthy as the GOP tax bills take shape
newBody: Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) said Monday she hopes "very much to be able to support a tax reform package," but laid out some specific things she wants to see in the legislation. "I do not believe that the top rate should be lowered for individuals who are making more than $1 million a year," Collins told Bloomberg News. "I don't think there's any need to eliminate the estate tax." House Republicans are unveiling their tax bill on Wednesday, and the Senate bill, expected a week later, will be more tailored...

issue: Susan Collins Announces Opposition to Tax Cuts for the Wealthy
roundup: Susan Collins announced that she will oppose the GOP tax plan if it cuts taxes for the wealthy or eliminates the estate tax. The House will release the bill on November 1st, and the Senate will produce a modified version next week.

left.newsTitle: House Republicans set to (supposedly) roll out their slapped together plan to cut taxes for the rich
newBody: House Republicans are set to "definitely" roll out their plan to cut taxes for the wealthy on Thursday. This is after the definite roll out for Wednesday was delayed because they’re still fighting over the details of this plan that’s been slapped together behind closed doors.

right.newsTitle: Rep. Steve Scalise: Even those in high-tax states will see ‘a real tax cut’
newBody: House Majority Whip Steve Scalise said Thursday those in high-tax states will also be better off under the Republican plan.

center.newsTitle: Republicans Stick With Big Corporate Tax Cuts in House Bill
newBody: The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act seeks the biggest transformation of tax code in more than 30 years; leaves top individual tax rate at 39.6%

issue: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
roundup: House Republicans, seeking the biggest change in the U.S. tax code in more than 30 years, aim to reduce the corporate tax rate from 35% to 20%, compress the number of individual income tax brackets, and repeal the taxes paid by large estates starting in 2024.

left.newsTitle: Rick Perry actually tried to argue that fossil fuels can help fight sexual assault
newBody: This is not the Onion.

right.newsTitle: The Hill's stupid coverage of Rick Perry's sexual assault comment is why nobody trusts the media
newBody: It's almost the perfect tweet for press coverage of the Trump administration. A Trump administration official makes a claim, poorly articulated, and a reporter wryly and snarkily reduces that argument to a stupid and overly simplistic format. The Hill — maybe the worst offender in this regard -- tweets out that reductive and misleading formulation, and it goes viral.

center.newsTitle: Perry links fossil fuel development to preventing sexual assault
newBody: Energy Secretary Rick Perry suggested Thursday that expanding the use of fossil fuels could help prevent sexual assault.

issue: Rick Perry Links Fossil Fuels with Decreased Sexual Assault, Draws Controversy
roundup: Rick Perry said on Thursday that the use of fossil fuels could prevent sexual assault in Africa. "But also from the standpoint of sexual assault. When the lights are on, when you have light that shines, the righteousness, if you will on those types of acts," he stated. Many on the Left criticized his remarks as insensitive, while some on the Right felt the media took it out of context.

left.newsTitle: It begins: Republican Congressmen introduce resolution calling for Mueller to resign
newBody: Fox News is going to be really into this.

right.newsTitle: GOP Reps. Gaetz, Gohmert, Biggs push for Mueller resignation in new resolution
newBody: Three GOP congressmen introduced a resolution Friday calling for special counsel Robert Mueller to resign from the Russia collusion probe, citing his ties to the FBI and its role in controversies involving Russia.

center.newsTitle: GOP lawmaker calls for Mueller recusal over uranium deal
newBody: A conservative House Republican is calling for Robert Mueller to resign as special counsel overseeing the FBI investigation of possible collusion between the Trump campaign and the Russian government.

issue: Congressmen Call for Mueller Resignation
roundup: Rep. Matt Gaetz, along with co-sponsors Rep. Andy Biggs and Rep. Louie Gohmert, introduced a resolution today that calls for special counsel Robert Mueller to resign from the Russia collusion probe. They cite his ties to the FBI as well as his involvement in the “Uranium One” controversy.

left.newsTitle: Bowe Bergdahl won’t serve prison time, and that’s making Trump really angry
newBody: Trump’s comments as a candidate may have influenced the judge to give Bergdahl a more lenient sentence.

right.newsTitle: The Bergdahl Sentence is a Travesty
newBody: A travesty of justice occurred on Friday. A deserter with blood on his heels will walk free, leaving dead and maimed Americans in his wake, because of a bully’s pulpit and a weak man’s bench and gavel. The miscarriage results from a president who tweets too much and a judge who discerns too little.

center.newsTitle: No prison for U.S. Army deserter Bergdahl, who Trump wanted dead
newBody: U.S. Army Sergeant Bowe Bergdahl on Friday was spared prison for endangering his comrades in arms when he deserted in Afghanistan in 2009, a sentence swiftly condemned by President Donald Trump, who while seeking election had called for his execution.

issue: Bowe Bergdahl Avoids Prison
roundup: Bowe Bergdahl will not serve any prison time for desertion, but will receive a dishonorable discharge. Trump had previously called for Bergdahl's execution, which the judge ruled a mitigating factor in the sentencing.

left.newsTitle: Trump Opens Asia Trip Talking Tough in Campaign-Style Rally
newBody: President Trump kicked off an extensive swing through Asia with a campaign-style rally on Sunday with American troops in Japan, as he looked toward a lengthy trip likely to be dominated by talks on confronting the nuclear threat from North Korea.

right.newsTitle: Trump ready for 'busy' leg of Asia trip, after informal talks in Japan on trade, North Korea
newBody: President Trump on Sunday discussed trade and North Korea problems over golf and dinner with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, as a prologue to the most critical stretch of the president’s 12-day Asia trip that starts Monday with formal talks in Tokyo.

center.newsTitle: Trump kicks off his 12-day tour of Asia in Japan
newBody: US President Donald Trump has landed in Japan, the first Asian country he is visiting during his 12-day tour of the region.

issue: Trump Kicks Off Asia Trip
roundup: President Trump kicked off his 12 day trip to Asia in Japan meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe to discuss trade and North Korea. President Trump has also said he would probably meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin while on the trip to discuss North Korea.

left.newsTitle: Paradise Papers leak: Documents reveal how the wealthy are hiding their money
newBody: A huge leak of financial documents revealed by a group of about 100 media organizations on Sunday provided deep insights into some of the mechanisms used by top politicians and celebrities to escape paying taxes.

right.newsTitle: The Paradise Papers: The Next Big Scandal To Hit Washington
newBody: Ok. What’s going on? Several news organizations have gotten their hands on leaked documents that have to deal with offshore accounts, tax havens and policies being influenced by some Trump associates and cabinet members.

center.newsTitle: Leaked documents reveal offshore dealings of top Trump officials
newBody: A slew of leaked documents reported by a consortium of news organizations show several individuals connected to President Trump as having legally protected their business investments or influenced policies that would keep client and company funds in tax havens.

issue: Trump Officials Linked to Offshore Accounts
roundup: Less than one week after Trump reiterated his promise to "bring back trillions of dollars from offshore", millions of leaked documents revealed that several Trump officials have used offshore accounts to keep company finances or personal investments in tax havens, including Rex Tillerson, Ben Carson, and Steve Mnuchin.

left.newsTitle: Air Force Error Allowed Texas Gunman to Buy Weapons
newBody: A day after a gunman massacred parishioners in a small Texas church, the Air Force admitted on Monday that it had failed to enter the man’s domestic violence court-martial into a federal database that could have blocked him from buying the rifle he used to kill 26 people.

right.newsTitle: Air Force launches review after failing to enter Texas shooter’s criminal history in FBI database
newBody:
He had a history of abusing his ex-wife and stepson as well as a bad-conduct discharge from the Air Force, yet the suspect in the Texas church massacre was able to obtain multiple firearms legally after passing background checks.

General Assembly this morning, taking its members to task for considering a vote to condemn the United States’ decision to move its embassy in Israel to Jerusalem. Here are some key excerpts from her powerful remarks, which focused on how the U.S. contributes far more to the U.N. and to international stability than any other nation.

center.newsTitle: U.N. General Assembly repudiates Trump on Jerusalem decision despite his threat of U.S. aid cutoff
newBody: The United Nations General Assembly voted overwhelmingly Thursday to repudiate President Trump’s controversial declaration recognizing Jerusalem as the capital of Israel. Trump threatened to withhold aid in retaliation for a vote condemning his position.

issue: UN Votes Against Trump's Jerusalem Decision
roundup: The United Nations voted 128-9 against President Trump's decision to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel despite his threat to cut aid to countries that expressed disapproval. Ambassador Nikki Haley said on Tuesday that she would be "taking names" of those who spoke out against the decision.

left.newsTitle: Trump Administration Considers Tearing Families Apart In New Immigration Crackdown
newBody: “Donald Trump’s war on immigrants has reached a sad new low. Separating families who are fleeing gang violence is unconscionable.”

right.newsTitle: Trump administration weighs policy that could split up families who enter US illegally
newBody: The Trump administration is considering a plan that could divide families that enter the U.S. from Mexico illegally, according to a new report.

center.newsTitle: ICE approves plan to separate families at border: report
newBody: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials have signed off on a plan to separate families who are caught crossing the U.S.-Mexico border illegally, officials close to discussions on the proposal told The New York Times.

issue: Trump Admin Considers New Immigration Plan
roundup: The Trump administration is considering a new immigration plan that would separate children from their parents when families are caught trying to cross the border illegally. ICE has approved the program, but Homeland Security Secretary Kirstjen Nielsen has yet to approve it.

left.newsTitle: 9th Circuit says Trump's third travel ban is illegal
newBody: A federal appeals court decided unanimously Friday that President Trump’s latest travel ban violates the law, but the ruling will not take effect until the Supreme Court reviews a likely appeal.

right.newsTitle: 9th Circuit court rules against third Trump travel ban, no immediate effect
newBody: The Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Friday that part of President Trump's third attempt at a travel ban should be blocked.

center.newsTitle: Trump doesn't have authority to issue a travel ban, appeals court rules
newBody: A federal appeals court in San Francisco ruled Friday night that the latest iteration of President Trump's travel ban violates federal law, and its issuance by the president via executive order exceeds executive branch authority as delegated by the Constitution.

issue: Appeals Court Rules Against Travel Ban
roundup: The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that President Trump's latest travel ban violates federal law by engaging in "nationality discrimination". The ruling will not go into effect until the Supreme Court hears the case.

left.newsTitle: 10 Weird Holiday Traditions Celebrated Around the World
newBody: Forget about Santa Claus. As the holidays approach, millions of people around the world will participate in their own holiday traditions. Instead of hanging stockings on the mantle or drinking eggnog around a fire watching holiday movies, there are other whacky traditions that people in different cultures partake in.

right.newsTitle: Christmas in Saudi Arabia
newBody: Mecca and Medina, Islam’s two holiest cities, are both located in Saudi Arabia. As guardians of these sacred sites, the Saudi royal family has decreed that no non-Muslim house of worship may be erected in the kingdom.

center.newsTitle: Whiskey And Fufu: What Kids Around The World Leave Out For Santa
newBody: Children all over the United States will have a big decision to make on Christmas Eve: Would Santa Claus prefer a chocolate chip cookie for a snack or perhaps a peanut butter and jelly sandwich?

issue: Christmas Around the World
roundup: Merry Christmas Eve! As the holiday approaches, take a look at some traditions around the globe.

left.newsTitle: Obama Warns Social Media Risks Splintering Society
newBody: Former U.S. president Barack Obama said the way people communicate via social media risked splintering society and leaders had to ensure the Internet did not cocoon users within their own biases.

right.newsTitle: Obama Warns of 'Dangers' of Internet, Social Media in Sitdown With Prince Harry
newBody: Former President Barack Obama warned about the "dangers" of the internet and social media in a sitdown with Great Britain's Prince Harry.

center.newsTitle: Obama issues warning on social media dangers in Prince Harry interview
newBody: Former President Obama issued a warning against "irresponsible" social media use in a wide-ranging interview with Britain's Prince Harry on Wednesday.

issue: Obama Warns About Social Media Risks
roundup: Former President Barack Obama warns that social media risks splintering society in an interview with Prince Harry.

left.newsTitle: 10 questions journalists never thought they'd have to ask
newBody: The president’s volatile temper and thin skin have prompted many improbable exchanges this year, including questions about neo-Nazis, slavery and morons

right.newsTitle: Media Coverage Marked By Bombshells That Weren’t
newBody: Establishment journalists claim that the Trump era has produced a “golden age” of journalism, but media coverage in 2017 was plagued with errors and “bombshells” that turned out to be anything but.

center.newsTitle: War between Trump, media set to intensify
newBody: Donald Trump’s unconventional presidency has roiled the media landscape, creating new dynamics that will play a major role in shaping his second year in office.

issue: 2017: The Media and Donald Trump
roundup: As 2017 comes to a close, a look at media coverage of Donald Trump.

left.newsTitle: Marco Rubio expresses doubts about the tax reform bill he just voted for
newBody: Sen. Marco Rubio, R-Fla., is publicly criticizing the same tax reform bill that he voted for.

right.newsTitle: Marco Rubio: Tax bill 'probably went too far' with helping corporations
newBody: Sen. Marco Rubio, R-Fla., believes the recently passed Republican tax plan “probably went too far” with helping big companies.

center.newsTitle: Sen. Marco Rubio thinks the GOP tax plan helps corporations too much
newBody: Sen. Marco Rubio says the GOP "probably went too far" in slashing the tax burden on corporations.

issue: Marco Rubio Expresses Doubts About Tax Bill
roundup: Marco Rubio expressed concern about the recently passed GOP tax bill in a new interview, stating that the plan went too far in helping corporations. "Some of them will be forced, because they’re sitting on historic levels of cash, to pay out dividends to shareholders. That isn’t going to create dramatic economic growth," he said.

left.newsTitle: Trump, the Reality Show President, Is Preparing an Overhaul of His White House Cast
newBody: Speculation is mounting about changes to the White House team as President Trump’s administration prepares itself for a surge of departures and arrivals over the holiday season.

right.newsTitle: White House shakeup in political department expected in the new year: Report
newBody: The White House political operation is expecting a reshuffling in the new year with senior Trump official Johnny DeStefano expected to take on a larger role, reported Axios on Thursday.

center.newsTitle: Scoop: White House reshuffle expected in new year
newBody: There's an operational reshuffle coming at the top level of the White House. Senior Trump administration official Johnny DeStefano is set to assume greater responsibilities and influence, including overseeing the beleaguered White House political operation.

issue: White House Staffing Changes
roundup: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to implement several staffing changes, with Johnny DeStefano expected to oversee the political department as well as take over most of deputy chief of staff Richard Dearborn's duties, who will be leaving in the new year.

left.newsTitle: Over 450 Protesters Arrested In Tehran During Crackdown On Anti-Government Demonstrations
newBody: Iran’s Supreme Leader accused enemies of the Islamic Republic of stirring unrest across the country.

right.newsTitle: Trump Blasts ‘Failing’ Iran Calls For Major Change
newBody: President Donald Trump harshly criticized the Islamic Republic of Iran Monday amid ongoing protests in the country.

center.newsTitle: Trump: Iranians ‘finally acting’ against ‘brutal and corrupt’ regime
newBody: President Trump on Tuesday said the Iranian people are “finally” taking action against the country’s “brutal and corrupt” rule, again warning its leaders that “the U.S. is watching.”

issue: Trump Blasts Iran as Protests Boil Over
roundup: As anti-government protests continue in Iran, President Trump tweeted that it is "time for change". He continued, stating that "the people of Iran are finally acting against the brutal and corrupt Iranian regime. All of the money that President Obama so foolishly gave them went into terrorism and into their 'pockets.' The people have little food, big inflation and no human rights. The U.S. is watching!"

left.newsTitle: OPINION: Kim Jong Un pitting South Korea against US by re-establishing talks
newBody: North and South Korea officially resumed direct contact through a military hotline on Wednesday, but while the move engendered optimism among many South Koreans, there are plenty of people on both sides of the globe questioning the motives of dictator Kim Jong Un.

right.newsTitle: As Trump Taunts Kim, NKorea Speaks With Seoul Over Hotline
newBody: North Korea contacted authorities in Seoul over a hotline for the first time in about two years, paving the way for a thaw during the Winter Olympics despite President Donald Trump's fresh taunts at Kim Jong Un.

center.newsTitle: North Korea reopens hotline to South to discuss Olympics
newBody: North Korea has reopened a hotline to South Korea, almost two years after it was disabled on the orders of leader Kim Jong-un.

issue: North Korea Opens Hotline to South Korea
roundup: North Korea Contacted Seoul over a hotline for the first time in almost two years. The call was to discuss the Winter Olympics, but some question the motives of Kim Jong Un.

left.newsTitle: Trump lawyer seeks to block insider book on White House
newBody: A lawyer representing President Trump sought Thursday to stop the publication of a new behind-the-scenes book about the White House that has already led Trump to angrily decry his former chief strategist Stephen K. Bannon.

right.newsTitle: Trump’s lawyer sends cease-and-desist letter to ‘Fire and Fury’ book publisher, author
newBody: The White House and its allies again pushed back aggressively Thursday against former adviser Steve Bannon and a new book that gives an unflattering portrayal of President Trump and his inner circle.

center.newsTitle: Trump Bannon row: Lawyers seek to halt book's release
newBody: Lawyers for US President Donald Trump are seeking to stop the release of a book containing explosive insights into his presidency.
Fire and Fury: Inside the Trump White House is due for release on Tuesday.

issue: Trump Lawyers Seek to Halt Book Release
roundup: The White House pushed back against Steve Bannon and a new book by Michael Wolff that gives an unflattering portrayal of President Trump. A cease-and-desist letter was sent while lawyers investigate "false statements."

left.newsTitle: Trump’s voting commission was doomed from the start
newBody: The foundation for President Trump's now disbanded voting commission was a conspiracy theory. And it only got more detached from reality from there.

right.newsTitle: Trump Ends His Voter Fraud Commission, Asks Homeland Security To ‘Review The Issues’
newBody: President Donald Trump decided to dissolve his commission on voter fraud Wednesday, citing refusal from states to cooperate with his commission.

center.newsTitle: Trump disbands controversial voting commission, citing 'endless legal battles'
newBody: President Trump signed an executive order late Wednesday disbanding his own election integrity commission after less than eight months, saying he didn't want to waste taxpayer money fighting with state governments over their voter data.

issue: Trump Disbands Voter Fraud Commission
roundup: President Trump disbanded his voter fraud commission on Wednesday after several state governments refused to turn over confidential voter data. The Department of Homeland Security will continue the investigation, which is probing voter fraud in the 2016 presidential election.

left.newsTitle: Bannon’s allies start to abandon him
newBody: Former White House chief strategist Steve Bannon’s hopes of leading a revolt in the Republican Party this year suffered a severe blow Thursday as his allies rebuked and abandoned him following a nasty public break with President Trump.

right.newsTitle: Trump-Bannon feud lays bare new fissure in GOP as prominent donor takes sides
newBody: The acrimony surrounding former White House adviser Steve Bannon's very public break with President Donald Trump has escalated, suggesting a permanent split between the president and the pugilistic strategist who helped put him in the Oval Office. The new fissure in an already fractious Republican Party cast doubt on Bannon's hopes to foment a movement centered on "Trumpism without Trump."

center.newsTitle: Bannon Fights for Survival
newBody: The fractured relationship between President Trump and his former chief strategist Stephen Bannon took center stage on Thursday as questions mounted about Bannon’s political future.

issue: Troubles Continue for Steve Bannon
roundup: Bannon's troubles continue as allies drift and prominent donors take sides.

left.newsTitle: Jeff Sessions Unleashes Federal Prosecutors On Legal Marijuana
newBody: The Justice Department is rolling back Obama-era rules that allowed states to cultivate legal marijuana industries.

right.newsTitle: Gary Johnson says Trump marijuana reversal could doom re-election
newBody: Former Libertarian presidential candidate Gary Johnson reacted angrily to President Trump's apparent abandonment of a campaign pledge to leave pot policy to the states, saying he hopes the pivot ends Trump's shot at re-election.

center.newsTitle: Marijuana businesses brace for investment chill as U.S. changes policy
newBody: Cannabis businesses across the United States said they are bracing for an investment slowdown following the U.S. Justice Department’s Thursday directive that will allow the enforcement of federal marijuana laws in states that have legalized the drug.

issue: Sessions Rescinds Obama-era Marijuana Rules
roundup: Jeff Sessions announced that the DOJ will allow prosecutors to enforce federal marijuana laws in states that have legalized the drug. Cannabis businesses across the country are preparing for a decline in investments, with stock prices in marijuana companies already starting to fall.

left.newsTitle: U.S. added 148,000 jobs in December, in lagging finish to year of strong growth
newBody: The U.S. economy added 148,000 jobs in December after a year of steady hiring, missing expectations for a larger last-minute surge, the government reported Friday.

right.newsTitle: Unemployment Holds Steady As Year Ends
newBody: Nearly 150,000 jobs were added last month while the unemployment rate remained steady from November, according to the Department of Labor’s December jobs report.

center.newsTitle: Jobs report: Employers added disappointing 148,000 jobs in Dec.
newBody: The labor market slowed in December as U.S. employers added 148,000 jobs in a sign that worker shortages may crimp hiring in 2018. The unemployment rate, which is calculated from a different survey, was unchanged at 4.1%, the Labor Department said Friday.

issue: December 2017 Jobs Report
roundup: The U.S. added 148,000 jobs in Dec., falling short of the 190,000 jobs expected. Unemployment remained at 4.1%, which is a 17 year low.

left.newsTitle: Senate will force vote on overturning net neutrality repeal
newBody: Senator Ed Markey (D-MA) has mustered the 30 votes necessary to force a vote on the FCC’s decision to repeal net neutrality. Senator Claire McCaskill (D-MO) announced that she’s signed onto Markey’s request to overturn the new rules, under the Congressional Review Act — which lets Congress nullify recently passed regulations with a simple majority.

right.newsTitle: Democrats try to bring back net neutrality
newBody: Democratic lawmakers said Monday that they have enough support to force a Senate vote on repealing the Trump administration's rollback of "net neutrality" regulations.

center.newsTitle: The effort to block the FCC's repeal of net neutrality just hit an important milestone
newBody: The effort to overturn the Federal Communications Commission's recent repeal of its net neutrality rules just crossed an important threshold.

issue: Senate to Vote on Net Neutrality Repeal
roundup: Thirty Democratic lawmakers have signed a resolution to overturn the FCC's recent net neutrality repeal, which is enough to force a vote on the measure. If it passes the Senate and the House, it will ultimately land on President Trump’s desk, who will make the final decision.

left.newsTitle: OPINION: Can South Korea Avoid Getting Played by the North?
newBody: The talks that opened this week between the North and South Korean governments are off to an inauspicious start: Even before negotiators could settle into their seats, the North had pocketed its first concession from the South, offering nothing in return.

right.newsTitle: North, South Korea agree to talks aimed at reducing military tensions
newBody: North Korea has agreed to "actively cooperate" with South Korea in talks to reduce military tensions ahead of next month's Winter Olympics in Pyeongchang.

center.newsTitle: North Korea, South Korea agree to hold military talks
newBody: North and South Korea agreed to hold military talks, a joint statement said after the two Koreas engaged in formal dialogue on Tuesday for the first time in more than two years.

issue: North Korea and South Korea Agree to Hold Military Talks
roundup: North and South Korea agreed to hold military talks, a joint statement said after the two Koreas engaged in formal dialogue on Tuesday for the first time in more than two years.

left.newsTitle: The fine print in the major DACA decision is a doozy
newBody: On Tuesday, a San Francisco federal district court judge enjoined—that is, blocked—Trump’s attack on the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, or DACA, program. This injunction is temporary, in place until the court rules on the substance—or the merits—of the challenge to Trump’s plan to terminate DACA.
The good news is by granting a preliminary injunction the judge has indicated that he thinks DACA’s backers are likely to prevail. The bad news is that the injunction isn’t complete.

right.newsTitle: Federal Judge Blocks Trump From Ending DACA
newBody: A federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from ending the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program on Tuesday, declaring that the Department of Homeland Security’s “decision to rescind DACA was based on a flawed legal premise."

center.newsTitle: Judge blocks Trump move to end DACA
newBody: A federal judge in San Francisco on Tuesday temporarily blocked the Trump administration from ending the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program that protects certain immigrants from deportation.

issue: Federal Judge Blocks Trump From Ending DACA
roundup: A federal judge in San Francisco temporarily blocked the Trump Administration from ending DACA, saying that the decision to rescind was based on a flawed legal premise.

left.newsTitle: Trump administration opens door to let states impose Medicaid work requirements
newBody: The Trump administration issued guidance to states early Thursday that will allow them to compel people to work or prepare for jobs in order to receive Medicaid for the first time in the half-century history of this pillar of the nation’s social safety net.

right.newsTitle: Trump administration opens door to allowing Medicaid work requirements
newBody: The Trump administration announced Thursday that it will open the door for states to impose work requirements for Medicaid recipients, in a major shift that could affect millions of low-income people receiving benefits.

center.newsTitle: Trump administration will allow states to test Medicaid work requirements
newBody: The Trump administration said on Thursday it would allow states to test requiring some Medicaid recipients to work or participate in community activities such as volunteering or jobs training as a condition of eligibility for the government health insurance program for the poor.

issue: White House to Allow States to Test Medicaid Work Requirements
roundup: The Trump Administration says it will allow states to test Medicaid work requirements. The policy comes as 10 states are already waiting for this permission.

left.newsTitle: Report: Trump Lawyer Paid Porn Actress $130,000 For Silence Just Before Election
newBody: A longtime Trump Organization lawyer reportedly negotiated the NDA in October 2016.

right.newsTitle: Trump rep, former porn star deny ‘hush money’ claims
newBody: A personal lawyer for President Trump and a former porn star both denied a late-Friday report claiming the adult-film actress was paid in exchange for her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump.

center.newsTitle: Trump Lawyer Arranged $130,000 Payment for Adult-Film Star’s Silence
newBody: A lawyer for President Donald Trump arranged a $130,000 payment to a former adult-film star a month before the 2016 election as part of an agreement that precluded her from publicly discussing an alleged sexual encounter with Mr. Trump, according to people familiar with the matter.

issue: Trump Lawyer Pays Adult-Film Star for Silence Surrounding Sexual Encounter with Mr. Trump
roundup: The Wall Street Journal broke a story reporting that President Trump's lawyer arranged a $130,000 payment to a former porn star a month before the presidential election to stay silent regarding a sexual encounter she allegedly had with Mr. Trump in 2006.

left.newsTitle: Trump warns he will withdraw U.S. from Iran nuclear deal if fixes not made
newBody: President Trump on Friday kept alive the Iran nuclear deal he detests by waiving sanctions for the third time, but he said he will not grant another reprieve unless the agreement is amended to permanently block a potential pathway for Iran to build nuclear weapons.

right.newsTitle: Iran protesters thank Trump, call for stronger sanctions
newBody: They are risking their lives to bring freedom to Iran, and vow to continue their protests.

center.newsTitle: U.S. ultimatum on nuclear deal, new sanctions draw Iran threat
newBody: Iran said on Saturday it would retaliate against new sanctions imposed by the United States after President Donald Trump set an ultimatum to fix “disastrous flaws” in a deal curbing Tehran’s nuclear program.

issue: New Sanctions on Iran
roundup: President Trump on Friday kept the Iran nuclear deal by waiving sanctions for the third time, but he said he will not grant another reprieve unless the agreement is amended to permanently block a potential pathway for Iran to build nuclear weapons. Additionally, the Treasury Department placed new sanctions on 14 people and entities for alleged offenses unrelated to Iran’s nuclear industry. Iran said on Saturday it would retaliate against the new sanctions.

left.newsTitle: DACA Participants Can Again Apply for Renewal, Immigration Agency Says
newBody: The federal government said on Saturday that it would resume accepting renewal requests for a program that shields from deportation young immigrants who were brought illegally to the United States as children.

right.newsTitle: DACA Renewal Applications Resume After Judge's Ruling
newBody: Yesterday, the Department of Homeland Security announced that it would resume the application renewal process for illegal aliens seeking protection from deportation after being brought into the United States as children. These “Dreamers”, as they are known in some circles, had previously been shielded from deportation under President Barack Obama’s executive order known as the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program (DACA).

center.newsTitle: DACA Recipients Can Apply For Renewal, Government Says
newBody: The Department of Homeland Security says it will once again accept renewal requests from recipients of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program in response to a court order.

issue: DACA Recipients Open to Apply for Renewal
roundup: The federal government announced it would start accepting renewal applications from DACA recipients after a judge ruled that President Trump did not have the proper legal authority to rescind parts of the Obama-era immigration program.

left.newsTitle: Steve Bannon testifies before the House Intelligence Committee
newBody: Steve Bannon appears before the House Intelligence Committee on Tuesday morning, supposedly to answer questions about his role in Trump’s campaign and any connection to Russian operatives. This comes after Bannon first described the meeting at Trump Tower between Trump’s top campaign staff and a group of Russian representatives as both “treasonous” and “unpatriotic”—and then went on to explain how to do secret meetings with the Russians correctly.

right.newsTitle: Steve Bannon testifies before House Intel Committee as part of Russia probe
newBody: Fallen former President Trump confidante Steve Bannon will testify to lawmakers behind closed doors Tuesday in his first appearance on Capitol Hill since he ran afoul of the administration over quotes attributed to him in a bombshell book.

center.newsTitle: Steve Bannon testifies for Russia probe: Five questions House Intel may ask
newBody: Former White House chief strategist Steve Bannon is expected to testify behind closed doors to the House Intelligence Committee on Tuesday as part of its investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election.

issue: Bannon Testifies Before House Intel Committee
roundup: Steve Bannon appears before the House Intelligence Committee to answer questions about his role in Trump's campaign and any connection to Russian operatives.

left.newsTitle: Trump Has Perfect Cognitive Test Score, White House Physician Says
newBody: President Trump’s White House physician said Tuesday that the president received a perfect score on a cognitive test designed to screen for neurological impairment, which the military doctor said was evidence that Mr. Trump does not suffer from mental issues that prevent him from functioning in office.

right.newsTitle: OPINION: Trump's healthy as a horse, America (whether you like it or not)
newBody: After listening to a news conference Tuesday by the White House physician discussing results of his exam of President Trump last week, it’s overwhelmingly clear that the president is healthy physically and mentally and fit for office.

center.newsTitle: Trump's medical sparks online 'girther' movement
newBody: US presidents regularly undergo physical examinations. It is not remarkable. However, the results of Donald Trump's recent medical check-up have sparked an online conspiracy theory - the girther movement.

issue: Trump Is in Excellent Health, According to White House Physician
roundup: President Trump's physical exam show him to be physically and mentally healthy, but he could benefit from more exercise.

left.newsTitle: Hey Aziz Ansari defenders, saying 'no' is more complex than you think
newBody: It took very little time for the same-old deeply dangerous rhetoric to rear its ugly head after the publication of a report accusing Aziz Ansari of sexual misconduct. In the anonymous report—published over the weekend by Babe—a woman shares her account the alleged misconduct which took place on a date in September 2017.

right.newsTitle: Feminists, Stop Bad Sex Before It Happens
newBody: Women are free to opt out of hookup culture if they don’t like what it offers them.

center.newsTitle: The Aziz Ansari takedown is a setback for the #MeToo movement
newBody: If the term "jump the shark" didn't already exist, it would need to be invented to describe the state of the #MeToo movement after the publication of (and lavish praise for) a lengthy essay recounting the lurid details of one woman's bad date with comedian Aziz Ansari.

issue: After Ansari Story, Outlets Debate #MeToo Movement
roundup: Aziz Ansari has come under fire after an article on babe.net accused him of sexual misconduct by an anonymous woman named 'Grace'. Although the encounter detailed in the piece was consensual, she alleges he did not properly read her nonverbal cues as signs that she was uncomfortable. Some on the Left agree that he is guilty of sexual assault, while many others are asking: Has the #MeToo movement gone too far?

left.newsTitle: Trump Denies Changing His Position on Border Wall
newBody: President Trump directly contradicted his own chief of staff on Thursday and said his position on building a wall between the United States and Mexico had not “evolved.”

right.newsTitle: Donald Trump Corrects John Kelly: ‘The Wall Is the Wall, It Has Never Changed or Evolved’
newBody: President Donald Trump corrected his Chief of Staff John Kelly after he said that the president had “evolved” on the wall.

center.newsTitle: Trump: Vision of border wall 'has never changed or evolved’
newBody: President Trump said on Thursday that his vision of a border wall with Mexico has “never changed or evolved,” pushing back on his own chief of staff’s comments during a closed-door meeting with lawmakers.

issue: Trump Says Vision of Border Wall Has Never Changed
roundup: President Trump says that his vision of a border wall has never changed or evolved, pushing back on comments by his chief of staff.

left.newsTitle: Trump Hands Out ‘Fake News Awards,’ Sans the Red Carpet
newBody: President Trump — who gleefully questioned President Barack Obama’s birthplace for years without evidence, long insisted on the guilt of the Central Park Five despite exonerating proof and claimed that millions of illegal ballots cost him the popular vote in 2016 — wanted to have a word with the American public about accuracy in reporting.

right.newsTitle: President Trump reveals winners of his ‘Fake News’ awards
newBody: President Trump revealed the winners of his self-proclaimed ‘Fake News’ awards Wednesday night on Twitter -- with The New York Times topping the list.

center.newsTitle: Trump presents 'fake news' awards for 10 stories — some of which really were false
newBody: President Trump gave out fake news "awards" to six news organizations Wednesday night, capping a much-hyped social media spectacle that matched Trump's penchant for showmanship with his disdain for the news media covering it.

issue: ’Fake News’ Award Winners are Revealed
roundup: President Trump revealed winners of his self-proclaimed "Fake News" awards on Twitter - and the New York Times topped the list.

left.newsTitle: Congress Likely Racing Toward a Government Shutdown
newBody: A bitterly-divided Congress hurtled toward a government shutdown this weekend in a partisan stare-down over demands by Democrats for a solution on politically fraught legislation to protect about 700,000 younger immigrants from being deported.

right.newsTitle: House passes spending bill; Senate leaves government in suspense over shutdown
newBody: Legislation faces uncertain fate in Senate.

center.newsTitle: Blame Game Ramps Up as Shutdown Draws Near
newBody: Hours after the House voted, debate in the upper chamber devolved into a partisan blame-game, with Democratic and Republican leaders digging in their heels, convinced that the other party would suffer the political consequences of a government funding lapse.

issue: Government Shutdown Is Looming
roundup: The House passed a stopgap spending bill; now the Senate needs to pass the bill in order to avoid a shutdown.

left.newsTitle: Trump’s new HHS office will protect health care workers who object to abortion
newBody: The new “Conscience and Religious Freedom” division is being cheered by the religious right.

right.newsTitle: Trump Administration Creates Office To Protect Health Care Workers From Violating Religious Convictions
newBody: The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) announced Thursday it created a new division in charge of protecting health care workers so they don’t have to provide services that go against their religious or moral convictions.

center.newsTitle: Trump administration creates new religious, moral protections for health workers
newBody: The Trump administration has created new protections for health workers who have religious and moral objections to certain procedures, such as abortion or assisted suicide.

issue: Trump Admin Creates Conscience and Religious Freedom Office
roundup: The Trump administration announced the new Conscience and Religious Freedom Office which creates new protections for health care providers who have religious objections to certain procedures, such as abortion, transgender therapy, and assisted suicide.

left.newsTitle: On The Anniversary Of Trump’s Inauguration, The Government Is Shut Down
newBody: “We will no longer accept politicians who are all talk and no action,” he proclaimed at his inauguration.

right.newsTitle: Illegal immigrants cheer as Dreamer shutdown hits
newBody: Democrats called it the Trump shutdown. Republicans labeled it the Schumer shutdown. But in reality, it was the Dreamer shutdown.

center.newsTitle: Senate rejects funding bill, partial shutdown begins
newBody: Senators voted late Friday to reject a House-passed bill that would have funded the government until Feb. 16, beginning a partial government shutdown.

issue: Senate Rejects Bill, Government Shutdown Begins
roundup: Senators voted late Friday to reject a House-passed bill that would have funded the government until February 16. Although the voting did not fall completely along party lines, most Democrats voted against the bill in hopes of negotiation on "Dreamers," while many Republicans were making arguments related to child healthcare funding. Many on the Left are blaming the Trump administration and Republicans for the shutdown, while those on the Right blame Democrats and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.

left.newsTitle: Trump launches new round of partisan attacks as government shutdown enters Day 2
newBody: President Trump pressured Congress Sunday to end the government shutdown that reached its second day, attacking Democrats and urging Republicans to change the rules of the Senate if the standoff isn’t resolved.

right.newsTitle: Trump urges Senate Republicans to go nuclear to pass a budget if shutdown continues
newBody: President Trump called for Republicans to exercise the nuclear option to pass a long-term budget with a simple majority in the Senate, should the government shutdown continue for too long.

center.newsTitle: To end government shutdown, Trump suggests Senate use 'nuclear option'
newBody: As the partial government shutdown stretches into its second day, President Trump brought up one of his favorite suggestions to break the logjam: End the Senate rule that requires 60 votes for legislation to pass.

issue: Trump Floats Nuclear Option
roundup: As Day 2 of the government shutdown begins, President Trump suggested that Republicans use the nuclear option, which would allow the Senate to pass the funding bill with a simple majority.

left.newsTitle: OPINION: Ahead of key vote, both parties weigh risks and rewards
newBody: Democratic and Republican leaders are making intricate political calculations ahead of a planned 12 p.m. ET vote in the Senate on whether to end the government shutdown.

right.newsTitle: Democrats reject last-minute deal; Republicans schedule Monday vote to reopen government
newBody: Senators were reaching for a deal overnight Sunday to try to end a 2-day-old government shutdown, hoping to prevent the worst of the effects of furloughs that hits in earnest on Monday.

center.newsTitle: Shutdown grinds into workweek after Senate fails to clinch deal
newBody: The shutdown is barreling into the workweek after senators failed late Sunday to clinch a deal to reopen the government.

issue: Day 3 of Government Shutdown
roundup: President Trump blames Democrats as they reject a last-minute deal to reopen the government on Sunday night. Now, both Republicans and Democrats are weighing risks and rewards ahead of a vote at noon today.

(A substantial number of existing DACA protections for undocumented individuals brought to the U.S. as children begin expiring March 5.) That “promise,” to be clear, is not formally binding; Democrats’...

Five members of the minority caucus already broke ranks on Friday to vote in favor of the House-passed spending bill, meaning that a simple majority of the US Senate was on the record in support of the GOP's government funding bill. A number of the tiny handful of Republicans who voted with Democrats last week publicly lined up behind...

center.newsTitle: Senators strike deal to end government shutdown

center.newsTitle: Pennsylvania court tosses congressional boundaries; impact possible on 2018 election
newBody: Pennsylvania's highest court added its voice Monday to a growing chorus of federal and state judges that have struck down election maps drawn to help the political party in power.

issue: Pennsylvania Court Rules Gerrymandered Maps Unconstitutional
roundup: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that the state's congressional district map was unfairly gerrymandered to benefit the GOP and that it must be redrawn before the 2018 midterm elections.

newBody: President Donald Trump slapped steep tariffs on imports of solar panels and washing machines, kicking off his second year in office by showing he is ready to start implementing his long-promised “America First” trade policy.

issue: President Trump Imposes Tariffs on Solar Panels and Washing Machines

center.newsTitle: Democrats withdraw offer to fund Trump's border wall

issue: Offer to Fund Border Wall Withdrawn
roundup: After Senator Schumer rescinds an offer to fund the border wall, President Trump responds that there will be no DACA deal.

left.newsTitle: These Right-Wing Californians Are So Pissed Off They Want to Secede

right.newsTitle: Fed up with ‘tyranny’ and taxes, California group wants to secede from state

center.newsTitle: New California? 5 times Californians failed to split the Golden State

issue: Group Proposes California Secession
roundup: A group of right-leaning Californians proposed that part of the state secede and become "New California", composed primarily of rural areas. The large cities and coastal areas would remain intact, which the group says are ungovernable after “years of over taxation, regulation, and mono-party politics.”

left.newsTitle: Supervisors Vote 10-1 To Rename Columbus Day To Indigenous Peoples' Day

right.newsTitle: Columbus Day out, as U.S. DNA chipped by PC once more
newBody: San Francisco’s Board of Supervisors just voted to rename Columbus Day as Indigenous Peoples day as a means of honoring those people — those Indians-slash-Native-Americans-slash-Aboriginals-slash-indigenous-slash-what-have-you people — who lived in this country prior to its European settlement.

center.newsTitle: San Francisco votes to celebrate Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day
newBody: San Francisco’s primary legislative body voted Tuesday to replace Columbus Day with Indigenous Peoples Day in order to recognize the “historic discrimination and violence” against Native Americans in the U.S.

issue: SF Renames Columbus Day 'Indigenous Peoples Day'
roundup: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted to change Columbus Day to Indigenous Peoples Day in order to honor Native Americans who have faced “historic discrimination and violence” in the U.S. Many on the Left celebrate the decision as a victory, while many on the Right argue that it is a politically correct move that strips America of its national identity.

left.newsTitle: Trump, the anti-globalist, declares America 'open for business' in speech to globalists
newBody: President Trump on Friday made his salesman's pitch for America before an international crowd of corporate and political titans, and took credit for its economic success, yet he was shadowed by clouds from home — news of his heightened jeopardy in the Russia probe and opposition to his immigration plan.

right.newsTitle: Trump at Davos: America Is 'Open for Business'
newBody: Speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Friday, President Trump told the gathering of political and business leaders about his “America First” policies, which have made the country competitive once again.

center.newsTitle: Davos: Trump launches attack on 'predatory' trade
newBody: President Donald Trump has launched a fierce attack on "predatory" trade practices, warning trading partners at the World Economic Forum in Davos that the US will not tolerate unfair trade.

issue: Trump at Davos: America First
roundup: In Davos, President Trump says that America is competitive again and open for business. He also warns against predatory trade practices.

left.newsTitle: Trump Immigration Plan Demands Tough Concessions From Democrats
newBody: President Trump proposed legislation on Thursday that would provide a path to citizenship for as many as 1.8 million young undocumented immigrants in exchange for an end to decades of family-based migration policies, a costly border wall and a vast crackdown on other immigrants living in the country illegally.

right.newsTitle: Trump immigration proposal could provide path to citizenship for 1.8 million in US illegally
newBody: The White House Thursday released an immigration plan that would offer a path to citizenship for approximately 1.8 million of the so-called "Dreamers," along with a $25 billion investment in border security -- including for President Trump's long-promised wall.

center.newsTitle: Trump offers 'Dreamers' a path to citizenship, wants other immigration curbs
newBody: U.S. President Donald Trump is offering a path to citizenship for up to 1.8 million young illegal immigrants but insists on measures that would curb some legal immigration programs and provide a border wall with Mexico, senior White House officials said on Thursday.

issue: Trump Offers Dreamers a Path to Citizenship
roundup: President Trump is offering a path to citizenship for 1.8 million Dreamers but insists on measures that would curb some immigration programs and provide for a border wall.

left.newsTitle: Watch As Sean Hannity Gets A Brutal Reality Check On Live TV

right.newsTitle: Sean Hannity: New York Times 'trying to distract' with report on Trump ordering Mueller's ouster
newBody: Fox News host Sean Hannity said on his program Thursday evening that the New York Times is trying to "distract" with its report that President Trump ordered special counsel Robert Mueller to be fired in June 2017.

center.newsTitle: Sean Hannity scoffs at reports that Trump tried to fire Mueller, then backpedals after a Fox News correspondent confirms it
newBody: Following a New York Times report where President Donald Trump reportedly ordered special counsel Robert Mueller fired one month after he was chosen to oversee the Russia investigation, Fox News host Sean Hannity came out swinging on his program Thursday night.

issue: Hannity Backtracks on New York Times Report

Many on the Left have criticized the host's reporting on the Trump-Russia probe, while many on the Right feel that coverage of the investigation is a distraction.

left.newsTitle: As Republicans Attack The DOJ And FBI, Sessions Vows To Stand Up To ‘Unfair’ Criticism
newBody: GOP politicians have been questioning the integrity of the nation’s premier law enforcement agency in an effort to undermine the Mueller probe.

right.newsTitle: Sessions vows to eliminate political bias at DOJ
newBody: Attorney General Jeff Sessions said Friday he’s determined to eliminate “political bias” from the Justice Department, and said the department must be more open to the kind of criticism it’s facing from Congress right now.

center.newsTitle: Sessions vows to battle bias following FBI texting controversy
newBody: Attorney General Jeff Sessions on Friday pledged to fight bias at the Justice Department as some Republicans raise concerns about political prejudice among the ranks of the FBI.

issue: Sessions Vows to Fight Bias at DOJ
roundup: In a speech on Friday, Attorney General Jeff Sessions said his mission for the Justice Department was to enforce the law and that "it means absolutely eliminating political bias or favoritism – in either direction – from our investigations and prosecutions." These comments came after some Republicans had recently criticized the bias of the FBI, especially in relation to the Russia investigation.

left.newsTitle: Trump’s first State of the Union: Can a divisive president flip the script?
newBody: President Trump will deliver his first State of the Union address Tuesday at a juncture of opportunity and peril for his presidency, and his anxious allies hope he will show he has the ability to do something he has not done before: bring the country together.

right.newsTitle: Anti-Trump celebs plan 'People's State of the Union'
newBody: A group of Hollywood elites, progressive groups and social activists are planning a “People’s State of the Union” as a “public alternative” on the eve of President Donald Trump’s first State of the Union address.

center.newsTitle: 'Safe, strong and proud' will be message of Trump's first State of the Union, officials say
newBody: Coming off an appearance on the global stage, and facing more problems on the investigative front, President Trump is preparing a State of the Union address designed to outline his vision of a safer and stronger United States, officials said.

issue: Trump to Give First State of the Union
roundup: President Trump will deliver his first State of the Union address on Tuesday where he will outline the economic benefits of the tax cuts and will present his plans for immigration, infrastructure, and trade.

left.newsTitle: Trump just decided not to sanction Russia for its election meddling
newBody: But his Treasury Department did put out a list of Russian oligarchs and officials to “name and shame” them.

right.newsTitle: State Department: New sanctions are deterring Russian defense sales

center.newsTitle: Trump administration holds off on new Russia sanctions, despite law

issue: Trump Admin Not to Impose Russian Sanctions
roundup: The Trump administration announced that they will not impose new sanctions on Russia despite a bipartisan law passed last year that authorized such sanctions to punish Moscow for meddling in the 2016 election. State Department spokeswoman Heather Nauert said that the threat of additional sanctions has already deterred Russian defense sales so there is no need to impose them at this time.

center.newsTitle: FBI Warns Of 'Grave Concerns' About 'Accuracy' Of GOP Snooping Memo
newBody: The FBI said Wednesday it has "grave concerns" about the "accuracy" of the much discussed Republican memo alleging the bureau and the Justice Department abused their surveillance authorities to target the Trump campaign.

issue: FBI Warns Against Releasing FISA Memo
roundup: The FBI expressed "grave concerns" about the GOP memo that alleges the DOJ and the bureau abused surveillance capabilities to target the Trump presidential campaign saying that it contains "omissions of fact that fundamentally impact the memo’s accuracy."

roundup: San Francisco is dismissing thousands of marijuana convictions retroactively now that the city has legalized the drug, and thousands of felonies may be reclassified with reduced punishments.

right.newsTitle: Trump to Declassify Infamous FISA Memo

issue: Trump Accuses FBI and DOJ of Political Bias

left.newsTitle: Trump, in a panic over dud Nunes' memo, says Adam Schiff 'must be stopped'  By Mark Sumner   Monday

right.newsTitle: Trump slams 'Little' Adam Schiff as 'one of the biggest liars and leakers' in Washington

center.newsTitle: 2 senators offer bipartisan bill protecting young immigrants, but Trump quickly rejects it
