Chris Coons will introduce a bipartisan immigration bill that will grant legal status to "Dreamers" but will not provide funding for a border wall. President Trump tweeted on Monday that any bill without wall funding is a "total waste of time."

left.newsTitle: FEMA Contract Called for 30 Million Meals for Puerto Ricans. 50,000 Were Delivered.

right.newsTitle: Shutdown Less Likely as Senate Closes in on Budget Agreement

center.newsTitle: Senate nears two-year deal on spending

center.newsTitle: Shutdown averted as Trump signs budget bill

issue: Congress Passes and Trump Signs a 2-Year Spending Bill
roundup: President Donald Trump has signed a budget bill approved by Congress to re-open the government after it was briefly closed overnight. The bill will boost spending by about $300 billion over the next two years.

left.newsTitle: Trump Blocks Release of Memo Rebutting Republican Claims
newBody: President Trump on Friday blocked the release of a classified Democratic memo rebutting Republican claims that top federal law enforcement officials had abused their powers in spying on a former Trump campaign aide, a move that Democrats denounced as politically motivated hypocrisy.

right.newsTitle: White House Cites Security Concerns in Decision Not to Declassify the Democratic Memo
newBody: President Trump has decided not to declassify the Democratic rebuttal to a memo that details surveillance abuses at the FBI. Trump reviewed the rebuttal just as he did the Republican-authored memo, but decided against making it public because of national security concerns. He has asked the authors to remove some sensitive materials.

center.newsTitle: Trump blocks release of Russia memo drafted by Democrats
newBody: President Donald Trump on Friday blocked the release of a classified memo written by congressional Democrats to rebut a Republican document that he allowed to be made public last week that claimed FBI and Justice Department bias against him in the federal probe of Russia and the 2016 U.S. election.

issue: President Trump Denies Request to Release Democrats' Russia Memo
roundup: President Trump blocked the release of a Democratic memo that was written to rebut Republican claims that the FBI and DOJ abused surveillance powers to target Trump in the Russia probe. left.newsTitle: Trump is worried about lives “shattered...by a mere allegation” after two aides are accused of domestic abuse

right.newsTitle: ‘No Such Thing As Due Process?’ – Trump Weighs In On Domestic Abuse Allegations
newBody: President Donald Trump reacted to allegations that his former staff secretary Rob Porter abused two of his ex-wives, lamenting that accusations often amount to the end of one’s career in today’s media environment.

center.newsTitle: Donald Trump: Lives are being 'destroyed' by allegations
newBody: President Donald Trump says lives are being "destroyed by mere allegation" after two White House aides quit amid accusations of domestic abuse.

issue: Trump Tweets About Allegations and Due Process
roundup: President Trump tweeted on Saturday that "peoples lives are being shattered and destroyed by a mere allegation," and "there is no recovery for someone falsely accused ... is there no such thing any longer as Due Process?" after two White House aides quit amid accusations of domestic abuse. These tweets come amid a national and worldwide debate over sexual harassment and abuse.

left.newsTitle: Trump Plan to Overhaul U.S. Infrastructure Faces Steep Hurdles

right.newsTitle: Trump wants $1.5T infrastructure spending boost, cuts to red tape

center.newsTitle: White House to unveil $1.5 trillion infrastructure plan
newBody: The White House on Monday will unveil its long-awaited $1.5 trillion infrastructure package aimed at overhauling U.S. public works.

issue: The White House to Unveil a $1.5 Trillion Infrastructure Plan
roundup: The White House will unveil today a $1.5 trillion infrastructure plan that cuts red tape while facing hurdles in Congress.

left.newsTitle: Why Are Trump and the G.O.P. So Determined to Kill PBS?

right.newsTitle: Trump proposes cutting all federal funds for NPR, PBS

center.newsTitle: The Corporation for Public Broadcasting blasts White House over deep cuts to funding
newBody: The White House released its 2019 budget proposal Monday, which calls for cuts to programs like Medicaid while boosting military spending and designating money for the border wall. issue: Budget Proposes Defunding PBS, NPR

left.newsTitle: Trump calls on Senate to support Grassley immigration legislation

right.newsTitle: Democrats look for new grand bargain on immigration

center.newsTitle: McConnell keeps firm grip on immigration debate

Yes, Mr. Musk, 46, the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, could not help unloading on the news media — members of which have written articles, especially in recent months, about the many problems that have plagued his companies.

right.newsTitle: Elon Musk rants against media on Twitter, proposes website to rate journalists
newBody: Tesla CEO Elon Musk aired his frustration with the media on Wednesday, issuing a series of tweets calling out the “hypocrisy of big media companies” before floating the idea of starting a website which would allow the public to rate journalists. “The holier-than-thou hypocrisy of big media companies who lay claim to the truth, but publish only enough to sugarcoat the lie, is why the public no longer respects them,” Musk started out by tweeting.
Musk went on to claim that “journos are under constant pressure to get max...

center.newsTitle: Elon Musk plans to create a website for public to rate the press
newBody: The serial entrepreneur's new project will let the public rate "the core truth" of news articles. Elon Musk is apparently tired of "fake news" or perhaps bad press, so he's creating a new site called Pravda to let the public rate "the core truth" of articles and track credibility scores of journalists, editors and publications.

The interestingly named Pravda, which was also the name of a Russian communist propaganda broadsheet, means "truth" in Russian, and it will be somewhat akin to a Yelp for journalism. Musk, the founder of SpaceX...

issue: Elon Musk Website May Track Press Credibility
roundup: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, tweeted that he might start a website where "the public can rate the core truth of any article & track the credibility" of journalists and press. Reactions on Twitter and among the press were strong, with many press describing Musk's comments as rants that were self-motivated rather than a benevolent effort to improve the state of the media.

left.newsTitle: Harvey Weinstein has surrendered to authorities in New York
newBody: More than 80 women have come forward to report sexual misconduct by producer Harvey Weinstein since October of last year. He has been fired from his company, kicked out of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, and pushed out of the Directors Guild of America. But Weinstein had never faced any criminal charges in connection with the many allegations of sexual harassment and assault against him. Until now.
Weinstein surrendered to authorities in New York the morning of Friday, May 25, and was arraigned shortly thereafter. Bond was...

right.newsTitle: Hillary Clinton Pal Harvey Weinstein Charged With First-Degree Rape
newBody: Hollywood movie mogul and Hillary Clinton pal Harvey Weinstein, who was glorified by actors and Democrats for years, has officially been charged with first and third degree rape against one woman in New York. He's also been charged with forcing two other woman into giving him oral sex against their will. He turned himself into authorities Friday morning.
It was a scene not unlike the red carpet walks he used to do, further highlighting how far the disgraced Hollywood producer has fallen since dozens of women came forward in the...

center.newsTitle: Harvey Weinstein formally charged with rape and a criminal sex act; posts $1M bail
newBody: Disgraced film producer Harvey Weinstein has been released on $1 million dollar bail, following his arraignment Friday.
He was charged in Manhattan court with rape, criminal sex act and other sex charges stemming from encounters with two women.
Accused by more than 80 women, Weinstein  surrendered to the New York Police Department and Manhattan District Attorney's office Friday morning.
At the arraignment, Weinstein agreed to wear an electronic monitoring device, paid for at his own expense.

issue: Harvey Weinstein Under Arrest for Criminal Sex Charges
roundup: Harvey Weinstein, Hollywood producer, surrendered himself to the NYPD after several charges and numerous accusations have been brought against him. He has since been released on $1 million bail.

left.newsTitle: Conservatives Threaten Netflix Boycott Over Obama Deal: 'I Will Read the Bible Instead'
newBody: Some conservatives are threatening to boycott Netflix after the streaming giant announced Monday it signed former President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama to a multi-year development deal.

right.newsTitle: Netflix's politics under fresh scrutiny after exclusive deal with Obamas to produce content
newBody: Netflix solidified its reputation as a liberal entertainment powerhouse with the announcement Monday that former President Barack Obama and former first lady Michelle Obama have signed on to produce a raft of new programming for the content conduit under their Higher Ground Productions shingle, and some conservative consumers aren't happy about it.

center.newsTitle: Obama plans to use Netflix deal to stop political divisiveness
newBody: Former President Obama said Wednesday he plans to use his new production deal with Netflix to combat political divisiveness.

issue: Netflix Announces Deal With Obamas
roundup: After Netflix announced on Monday that it would partner with former President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama to create content for the streaming site, some have expressed concern over the media giant's political leanings, although Mr. Obama says he plans to promote stories that help bridge the political divide.

left.newsTitle: Keeping Summit Hopes Alive Suggests Kim Jong-un May Need a Deal
newBody: Ever since Kim Jong-un took over as the young, untested ruler of North Korea seven years ago, he has promised his country a future free from deprivation.

right.newsTitle: What comes next for Trump and North Korea?
newBody: President Trump is leaving the door open to a sit-down meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, despite abruptly canceling their previously planned summit this week over the authoritarian regime’s latest threat of nuclear war.

center.newsTitle: Korean leaders meet in surprise summit
newBody: The leaders of North and South Korea have met in the demilitarised border area between the two countries.

issue: Leaders of North and South Korea Have Second Meeting
roundup: The news broke Saturday morning that South Korea's Moon Jae-in and the North's Kim Jong-un have met for a second time in the Demilitarized Zone. This meeting comes as there is uncertainty on whether the summit between North Korea and the United States will take place. Journalists from the right and left explore the possibility of the summit as well as what the next steps are.

left.newsTitle: Trump Unbelievably Rips Dems For Immigrant Kids Being Separated From Parents
newBody: He’s the one who launched the policy.

right.newsTitle: Trump calls for Democrats to end ‘horrible law’ that he says separates children from parents at border
newBody: President Trump on Saturday called on Democrats to end a “horrible law” that he says separates children from their parents when they cross the border -- and also accused them of “protecting MS-13 thugs.”

center.newsTitle: Trump Draws Distance From Administration Migrant Policy That Has Separated Families
newBody: The Trump administration has come under fire for its policy of separating migrant children from their parents at the border.

issue: Trump Calls for End to Policy of Separating Immigrant Families
roundup: President Trump tweeted on Saturday to "put pressure on the Democrats to end the horrible law" that separates immigrant children from their parents. Publications on the Left have argued that Trump's attacks on Democrats are unfounded, since the policy comes from the Trump administration's Justice Department. Those on the Right have said that the "zero-tolerance" policy was put into place to deter illegal immigrants from coming to the U.S. This story comes amid much backlash for the recent revelation from a Health and Human Services official that the government was unable to locate nearly 1,500 children who had been released from its custody.

left.newsTitle: Trump hits China with $50B tariffs, investment restrictions
newBody: President Donald Trump is moving ahead with steps to protect U.S. intellectual property by punishing China with broad investment restrictions, litigation at the World Trade Organization and hefty tariffs on $50 billion worth of Chinese goods.

right.newsTitle: Trump to impose 25% tariffs on 'industrially significant technology' from China
newBody: The Trump administration on Tuesday moved forward with a plan to impose 25 percent tariffs on $50 billion of "industrially significant technology" from China ahead of a meeting to discuss a trade deal between the two countries that Trump says will be more fair to America.

center.newsTitle: Trump moves forward with tech limits, tariffs ahead of China trade meeting
newBody: The Trump administration on Tuesday said it is going ahead with actions to crack down on Chinese trade practices by June 30.

issue: White House to Impose Tariffs on China
roundup: The Trump administration on Tuesday announced that it will move forward with a plan to impose 25 percent tariffs on $50 billion of tech goods imported from China by June 30 as well as plans to apply broad limits on Chinese tech investment. This move comes ahead of Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross's visit to China this weekend for trade negotiations.

left.newsTitle: ABC cancels ‘Roseanne’ after its star, Roseanne Barr, went on a vitriolic and racist Twitter rant
newBody: ABC announced Tuesday that it canceled “Roseanne” after the show’s star, Roseanne Barr, went on a vitriolic and racist Twitter rant.

right.newsTitle: Tone-deaf MSNBC slammed for bringing on Joy Reid to discuss Roseanne Barr's social media slur
newBody: MSNBC provided viewers with one of the most tone-deaf moments in cable news history on Tuesday when Andrea Mitchell asked Joy Reid about a racist tweet that Roseanne Barr sent about former Obama aide Valerie Jarrett.

center.newsTitle: ABC Cancels ‘Roseanne’ Sitcom After Star’s Racist Tweet
newBody: ABC canceled the hit sitcom “Roseanne” after its star, Roseanne Barr, sent a racist tweet about a top aide to former President Barack Obama.

issue: ABC Cancels 'Roseanne' After Roseanne Barr Tweet Sparks Outrage
roundup: ABC has canceled the sitcom 'Roseanne' after its star, Roseanne Barr, sent an insulting tweet directed at former Obama aide Valerie Jarrett. Ms. Barr tweeted if the “Muslim brotherhood & planet of the apes had a baby = vj." Ms. Jarrett was was born in Iran and is Black.

left.newsTitle: With impeachment looming, scandal-plagued Eric Greitens resigns as Missouri governor
newBody: On Tuesday afternoon, following months of scandals, indictments in two separate criminal cases, and looming impeachment proceedings, Missouri Gov. Eric Greitens finally announced he would resign effective Friday. With Greitens’ departure, Lt. Gov. Mike Parson, a fellow Republican, will take his place.

right.newsTitle: Missouri's embattled Republican governor resigns
newBody: Governor Eric Greitens, mired in a scandal over an extramarital affair and allegations of campaign-finance violations, announced his resignation, effective Friday, at a hastily called news conference as an impeachment effort in the Legislature gained momentum.

center.newsTitle: Embattled Missouri Governor Eric Greitens resigns amid scandals
newBody: Missouri Governor Eric Greitens announced his resignation Tuesday afternoon, leaving behind him a brief and tumultuous legacy and moving on from his first public office with the continued prospect of criminal prosecution related to his 2016 campaign.

issue: Missouri Governor Eric Greitens Resigns
roundup: Missouri Governor Eric Greitens, mired in a scandal over an extramarital affair and allegations of campaign-finance violations, announced his resignation, effective Friday.

left.newsTitle: Walmart to offer employees a college education for $1 a day
newBody: Walmart, the country’s largest private employer, announced Wednesday that it will pay for its workers to go back to school — as long as they get degrees in business or supply-chain management.

right.newsTitle: Walmart to cover employees' college tuition, within limits
newBody: Walmart will begin subsidizing the cost of college for store workers who work toward company-selected degrees at schools that have teamed with the retailing giant.

center.newsTitle: Walmart announces new college education program for employees
newBody: Walmart on Wednesday announced that it would pay for its employees to get a college education with the employee only spending $1 a day for their studies, The Washington Post reported.

issue: Walmart Announces Program to Pay for Employees' College Tuition
roundup: Walmart announced that they will pay for employees to obtain a college education if they contribute $1 a day and major in business or supply-chain management.

left.newsTitle: Conservative Crank Dinesh D’Souza To Be Pardoned By Donald Trump
newBody: President Donald Trump on Thursday said he will issue “a full pardon” to Dinesh D’Souza, a conservative activist and provocateur who regularly peddles conspiracy theories.

right.newsTitle: BREAKING: President Trump Will Fully Pardon Dinesh D'Souza
newBody: President Trump announced Thursday morning he will grant conservative author, filmmaker and thought leader Dinesh D'Souza a full pardon.

center.newsTitle: Trump says will pardon conservative commentator D'Souza
newBody: President Donald Trump said he will grant a full pardon on Thursday to conservative commentator Dinesh D’Souza, who was sentenced in 2014 to five years of probation for federal campaign law violations.

issue: President Trump Will Pardon Dinesh D’Souza
roundup: President Donald Trump said he will grant a full pardon on Thursday to conservative commentator Dinesh D’Souza, who was sentenced in 2014 to five years of probation for federal campaign law violations.

left.newsTitle: The real immigration crisis isn’t “missing” children. It’s family separations.
newBody: Thousands of Twitter users spent the weekend asking #WhereAreTheChildren?

The viral hashtag sprang up in response to a now widely shared New York Times article noting that the federal government had been unable to make contact with 1,475 unaccompanied minors awaiting deportation hearings.
First things first: Despite reports to the contrary, those children are not “missing” or “misplaced.”
Immigration experts point out that these children are not in government custody, nor are they supposed to be. Instead, this is a population of minors who arrived at the US border unaccompanied...

right.newsTitle: Remember those brutal immigrant detention centers liberals tried to pin on Trump? It was all Obama
newBody: Liberals and even ostensibly objective journalists are experts at getting themselves outraged. But only if they think that an abuse is occurring under President Trump.

Over Memorial Day Weekend, former Obama White House speechwriter Jon Favreau attempted to pin the blame of the harsh and brutal conditions for children and families at immigrant detention centers on President Trump.
Favreau tweeted on Sunday, "Look at these pictures. This is happening right now, and the only debate that matters is how we force our government to get these kids back to their...

center.newsTitle: Fallacies on both sides in immigration debate
newBody: Since the government acknowledged last month that the Trump administration had lost track of nearly 1,500 immigrant children, the debate over what that means and who is to blame has roiled Twitter. Here’s a look at the partisan claims and a reality check behind the latest immigration fight:

issue: Fact Check: Reports Misleading on Status of Immigrant Children
roundup: Misleading reports that said 1500 immigrant children had been "lost" caused backlash and a viral hashtag, #WhereAretheChildren?. However, media had conflated multiple stories about immigration: those 1500 children had arrived at the border unaccompanied and were not supposed to be in government custody.

left.newsTitle: Donald Trump Says Samantha Bee Should Be Fired
newBody: The late-night host has apologized for using an expletive to refer to Ivanka Trump.

right.newsTitle: Trump Blasts Hollywood 'Double Standard' After Samantha Bee's Vulgar, Sexist Attack on Ivanka
newBody: Comedian Samantha Bee has apologized to Ivanka Trump and viewers for using a severe obscenity to describe her.

center.newsTitle: Trump calls for comedian Samantha Bee's firing after crude Ivanka comment
newBody: President Donald Trump waded further into television controversies on Friday, calling for comedian Samantha Bee to be fired after she made a vulgar comment about his daughter and White House adviser Ivanka Trump on her program.

issue: Trump Responds to Samantha Bee Comment
roundup: President Trump fires back at comedian Samantha Bee after she insults Ivanka Trump.

left.newsTitle: It was no surprise Trump's North Korea summit was canceled. It's no surprise that it's back on
newBody: A week ago, when President Trump’s much-ballyhooed super-summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was suddenly canceled, I wrote an editorial for The Times asking whether, “seriously, is anyone really shocked?” But just to be clear, I’m no more shocked by the fact that it is back on than I was that it was cancelled in the first place.

right.newsTitle: On North Korea, Trump is wisely following Reagan's example
newBody: Now that his summit with North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un is back on for June 12 in Singapore, President Trump will benefit from some important lessons he appears to have learned by studying the success of President Reagan in dealing with the Soviet Union’s final leader, Mikhail Gorbachev.

center.newsTitle: Trump makes an about-face, revives summit with North Korean leader
newBody: President Donald Trump, in a complete reversal, said on Friday he would hold a summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on June 12 in Singapore in the latest twist in the high-stakes diplomacy over eliminating Pyonyang’s nuclear arms program.

issue: United States and North Korea Summit Back On
roundup: President Trump announced on Friday that the previously planned June 12 summit in Singapore with North Korea leader Kim Jong-un would be happening. Publications from the Right and Left offer their opinions on the summit being reinstated.

left.newsTitle: Trump’s Lawyers Argue It’s Not Possible For The President To Obstruct Justice
newBody: A 20-page letter sets up a possible battle for the president’s testimony in the Russia investigation.

right.newsTitle: Robert Mueller needs to 'man up,' avoid pulling 'another Comey' as Russia probe wraps up, Giuliani says
newBody: Special Counsel Robert Mueller is sensitive to pulling "another Comey" as the Russia probe enters its final months, Trump attorney Rudy Giuliani said in an interview Sunday.

center.newsTitle: Trump's lawyer says will fight Russia probe subpoena: report
newBody: U.S. President Donald Trump’s lead attorney said that if the special counsel investigating Russia’s alleged meddling in the 2016 U.S. election were to subpoena the president, it would set off a legal battle, according to an ABC News report on Saturday.

issue: Trump Legal Team Challenges Potential Subpoena in Russia Probe
roundup: President Trump's legal team sent a letter to special counsel Robert Mueller saying that Trump is not compelled to testify if subpoenaed, and that he could not have obstructed justice since he "has Constitutional authority to direct the Justice Department to open or close an investigation, and, of course, the power to pardon any person before, during, or after an investigation and/or conviction.” Trump's head lawyer, Rudy Giuliani, has said he will challenge any subpoena in court.

left.newsTitle: Parkland Students Are Taking Their Activism on the Road This Summer With a 20-State Bus Tour
newBody: It’s not going to be a quiet summer off for the students of Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School. With the school year ending, many of the Parkland school shooting survivors are taking their political activism on the road.

right.newsTitle: Parkland Students to Announce Nation-Wide Gun-Control Tour
newBody: The student gun control activists of Parkland will announce an extensive bus tour Monday featuring 70 stops in 20 states, where the students will advocate stricter gun control legislation and register voters to that end.

center.newsTitle: Parkland students' bus tour targets places where NRA 'bought and paid for politicians'
newBody: A group of students-turned-activists from Florida's Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School will be hitting the road next week on a nationwide bus tour aimed at educating voters — and encouraging them to actually vote to end gun violence.

issue: Parkland Students to Launch Gun Control Bus Tour
roundup: Students from Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School are launching a nationwide bus tour to increase voter registration, advocate for gun control, and campaign against the NRA.

left.newsTitle: I represented the wedding cake couple. We lost a battle but won the war.
newBody: In law, as in less civil arenas of conflict, you can lose a battle but win the war. That’s what happened in Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission, the case pitting

right.newsTitle: Religious freedom lives to fight another day
newBody: “Freedom of religion and religion has been used to justify all kinds of discrimination throughout history,” said Colorado Civil Rights Commissioner Diann Rice, “whether it be slavery, whether it be the Holocaust, whether it be …” Here she trailed off.

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court Ruling Ducks Conflict Between Religious, Gay Rights
newBody: The Supreme Court ducked deciding whether religious merchants have a constitutional right to deny service to gay people, but did rule Monday that a Christian baker didn’t get a fair hearing before a state civil-rights commission and therefore shouldn’t be penalized for turning away a same-sex couple.

issue: Supreme Court Rules in Favor of Christian Baker in Wedding Cake Dispute
roundup: The Supreme Court on Monday ruled in favor of Christian baker Jack Phillips who refused to make a wedding cake for a gay couple. Some on the Left have said that the verdict is somewhat of a victory, as the Court's majority opinion does not sanction a First Amendment right to discriminate, but instead says that the Colorado Civil Rights Commission displayed a bias against Mr. Phillips' faith in his initial hearing. Many on the Right celebrated the decision as a victory for religious freedom.

left.newsTitle: Mueller accuses Manafort of witness tampering
newBody: The Special Counsel's Office has accused former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort of attempting to get witnesses to lie for him in court, and they've asked the judge to send him to jail as he awaits his trial, according to a filing in DC District Court Monday night.

right.newsTitle: Robert Mueller prosecutors accuse Paul Manafort of attempting to tamper with witnesses
newBody: Special counsel Robert Mueller’s team has accused former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort of tampering with witnesses in his upcoming Washington, D.C., criminal trial, according to documents filed with the court late Monday.

center.newsTitle: Prosecutors: Paul Manafort tried to coach witnesses in criminal case
newBody: The FBI says that former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort attempted to tamper with witnesses — even going so far as to allegedly coach their testimony — in a federal tax and lobbying case against him.

issue: Mueller Accuses Manafort of Witness Tampering
roundup: The Special Counsel's Office has accused former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort of attempting to get witnesses to lie for him in court, and they've asked the judge to send him to jail as he awaits his trial.

left.newsTitle: Trump tried to make the Philadelphia Eagles a culture war. Then Fox News fumbled it.
newBody: Fox News tried to run with Trump’s lies about the Eagles. It ended up insulting Christians.

right.newsTitle: No, the Philadelphia Eagles didn't kneel during the national anthem
newBody: On Monday, President Trump disinvited the Super Bowl winning Philadelphia Eagles football team to the White House over an apparent disagreement over what players should be doing when the national anthem is played.

center.newsTitle: Trump Turns Philadelphia Eagles Event Into 'Celebration Of America'
newBody: There was God Bless America, but no Swoop the Eagle. The U.S. Marine Band was there, but neither quarterback Nick Foles, nor head coach Doug Pederson, nor any member of the 2018 Super Bowl winning team was at the White House Tuesday for what was to be a celebration of the Philadelphia Eagles victory.

issue: President Trump Cancels Philadelphia Eagles White House Visit
roundup: After several Philadelphia Eagles players pulled out of an upcoming White House visit, President Trump disinvited the team, citing differences over National Anthem protests. Several publications have emphasized that no Eagles players kneeled during the anthem throughout the season, contrary to a Fox News report which incorrectly stated otherwise.

left.newsTitle: 5 Takeaways From Tuesday’s Primary Elections
newBody: The battle for control of Congress was front and center on Tuesday night, with races taking shape in several intensely contested House seats in California and New Jersey. But there were revealing elections in the Midwest and the South, too, underscoring President Trump’s power in the Republican Party and the different ways Democrats hope to loosen his hold on red-state America.

right.newsTitle: Trump-backed John Cox outpaces Villaraigosa for Governor, Feinstein takes top spot in California Senate contest
newBody: Republican John Cox has secured a spot on the ballot to face Democratic Lieutenant Governor Gavin Newsom in the California gubernatorial election in November.

center.newsTitle: Six takeaways from 2018's Super Tuesday
newBody: Voters in seven states cast their ballots Tuesday in what amounts to the most significant primary election of the 2018 season, a Super Tuesday for partisans battling for control of Congress.

issue: California and New Jersey Primary Election Results
roundup: The battle for control of Congress was front and center on Tuesday night, with House and Senate races taking shape in California and New Jersey. In addition, Republican John Cox has secured a spot on the ballot to face Democratic Lieutenant Governor Gavin Newsom in the California gubernatorial election in November.

left.newsTitle: California Voters Remove Aaron Persky, the Judge Who Gave a 6-Month Sentence for Sexual Assault
newBody: Aaron Persky, the California judge who drew national attention in 2016 when he sentenced a Stanford student to just six months in jail for sexually assaulting an unconscious woman, was recalled on Tuesday, according to The Associated Press. He is the first judge recalled in California in more than 80 years.

right.newsTitle: Recalling Aaron Persky, the Judge Who Showed Brock Turner Leniency, Is a Mistake That Will Haunt Progressives
newBody: California voters just encouraged judges to show no mercy.

center.newsTitle: Voters remove California judge criticized over rape sentencing
newBody: Californians voted in a special election to unseat a state judge who drew worldwide condemnation for giving a six-month jail sentence to a Stanford University swimmer convicted of sexually assaulting an unconscious woman.

issue: Voters Recall California Judge Who Presided Over Brock Turner Rape Case
roundup: Residents of Santa Clara, California voted to recall Judge Aaron Persky, who controversially sentenced Stanford student Brock Turner to six months in prison after he was found guilty of sexually assaulting an unconscious woman. While some celebrated the decision, many on both sides of the aisle have argued that it is a setback for criminal justice, as it will encourage judges to impose harsher sentences on all defendants for fear of public backlash.

left.newsTitle: Senate Republicans claim that Obama secretly helped Iran get around US sanctions
newBody: “The Obama administration misled the American people and Congress because they were desperate to get a deal with Iran,” said one senator.

right.newsTitle: Obama administration allegedly gave Iran access to US financial system
newBody: The Obama administration granted a license letting Iran access the United States financial system despite officials’ pledges that they would prohibit it, according to a draft report from the Senate’s Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

center.newsTitle: Secret Obama-era permit let Iran convert funds to dollars
newBody: After striking an elusive nuclear deal with Iran, the Obama administration found itself in a quandary in early 2016: Iran had been promised access to its long-frozen overseas reserves, including $5.7 billion stuck in an Omani bank.

issue: Obama Administration Granted Iran Secret License to Access U.S. Financial System
roundup: The Obama administration allegedly gave Iran a license to access the U.S. financial system after striking the nuclear deal, despite public officials' promises that this wouldn't happen, according to a new report by Senate Republicans. The plan never came to fruition, as two U.S. banks would not participate.

left.newsTitle: DOJ watchdog finds James Comey defied authority as FBI director, sources say
newBody: The Justice Department's internal watchdog has concluded that James Comey defied authority at times during his tenure as FBI director, according to sources familiar with a draft report on the matter.

One source told ABC News that the draft report explicitly used the word "insubordinate" to describe Comey's behavior. Another source agreed with that characterization but could not confirm the use of the term.
In the draft report, Inspector General Michael Horowitz also rebuked former Attorney General Loretta Lynch for her handling of the federal investigation into Hillary Clinton's personal...

right.newsTitle: DOJ watchdog draft finds James Comey was sometimes 'insubordinate'
newBody: The Justice Department’s Office of the Inspector General reportedly found that former FBI Director James Comey at times defied his superiors while leading the bureau.

ABC News reported that a draft report from the department’s internal watchdog described Comey’s behavior as “insubordinate.” Sources told the outlet that the draft report also criticized former Attorney General Loretta Lynch for her handling of the probe into former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton’s use of a private email server.
The forthcoming report from the Justice Department’s internal watchdog is expected to detail the...

center.newsTitle: The White House is about to snag a major victory in its war against Comey and the FBI
newBody: The Department of Justice's inspector general has concluded that James Comey defied authority at times during his time leading of the FBI, ABC News reported Wednesday, citing sources familiar with a draft report on the matter.

The report, when finished and officially released, will cap Inspector General Michael Horowitz's inquiry into the FBI's handling of its investigation of Hillary Clinton's use of a private email server while she was secretary of state. The report is said to focus on senior FBI leadership at the time, like Comey and Attorney General...

issue: DOJ Report Finds Comey "Insubordinate", Rebukes Lynch
roundup: A draft report from the Department of Justice finds that FBI Director James Comey defied authority, reportedly using the term "insubordinate", and rebukes Attorney General Loretta Lynch's behavior during the federal investigation of former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton's use of a private email server.

left.newsTitle: Senator Warren pushes for federal clarity on marijuana
newBody: US Senator Elizabeth Warren Thursday unveiled legislation that would allow states to set their own marijuana policies without the threat of federal interference.

right.newsTitle: Sens. Gardner and Warren promote bill to bring marijuana businesses 'out of the shadows'
newBody: Sen. Cory Gardner and Sen. Elizabeth Warren crafted a bill to strengthen states’ right regarding marijuana legalization, they said in an interview Thursday with “Morning Joe.”

center.newsTitle: Senators introduce bipartisan bill to protect state laws on marijuana
newBody: Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Cory Gardner (R-Colo.) introduced a bipartisan bill on Thursday that would allow states to regulate marijuana without federal interference.

issue: Senators Announce Bipartisan Bill to Protect States' Rights on Marijuana Laws
roundup: Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Republican Sen. Cory Gardner introduced a bipartisan bill on Thursday that would prevent the federal government from infringing on marijuana laws in states that have legalized the drug.

left.newsTitle: Trump's Surprise Idea to Add Moscow to the G7
newBody: President Trump said Friday Russia should be readmitted to the Group of Seven industrialized nations, which the country was suspended from after its invasion and annexation of Ukraine’s Crimean peninsula in 2014. He made the remarks as he prepared to head to Canada for the annual G7 summit, and they add to a list of positions that put the U.S. in opposition to many of its allies ahead of what will likely be a bruising meeting over trade, Iran, and other issues.
“It used to be the G8 because Russia...

right.newsTitle: Trump Says 'Let Russia Back in' as He Heads for G-7 Summit
newBody: President Donald Trump injected fresh drama into an already tense meeting of the Group of Seven major industrialized nations Friday, calling for Russia, ousted for its the annexation of Crimea, to be reinstated.
Trump made the comment at the White House Friday after hours of further escalating his rhetoric against longtime allies over U.S. trade practices.
"Why are we having a meeting without Russia in the meeting? Trump said. "They should let Russia come back in because we should have Russia at the negotiating table."
Solidifying his solo status on...

center.newsTitle: Trump Wants Russia Back In G-7
newBody: President Trump is calling on the G-7 to re-admit Russia to the group of leading economic powers, saying "we should have Russia at the negotiating table."

Moscow was kicked out of the group, then the G-8, four years ago after it annexed Crimea. It had been invited to join the group in the 1990s after the collapse of the Soviet Union. But after Russia's intervention in Ukraine and annexation of Crimea, Western leaders sought to isolate Vladimir Putin's government.
Trump, talking to reporters as he left the White House for...

issue: Trump Says Russia Should Be Back in the G-7
roundup: President Trump called for Russia to be readmitted to the G-7 as he headed to the group's upcoming summit. In 2014, Russia was ousted after it annexed Crimea. Critics say that this comment could distance the U.S. from longtime allies, particularly after recent tensions about trade policy.

left.newsTitle: Trump calls for elimination of tariffs, end to US being world's 'piggy bank'
newBody: President Donald Trump on Saturday said he wanted to see the elimination of trade barriers between the United States and its closest allies, amid tensions over the Trump administration's move to impose steep tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from the EU, Canada and Mexico.

right.newsTitle: Trump pushes free trade at G7 days after imposing tariffs
newBody: President Trump preached a free-trade gospel in an impromptu press conference Saturday as he skipped out early on the annual G7 meeting in Quebec.

center.newsTitle: Trump demands end to 'unfair' trade after G7 summit
newBody: U.S. President Donald Trump told Group of Seven leaders that the United States wanted a quick end to trade practices that he says have led to an exodus of American companies and jobs to other countries.

issue: President Trump Calls for End to Tariffs at G7 Summit
roundup: President Trump called for an end to trade barriers and tariffs at the G7 summit, saying that the U.S. has been subjected to unfair trade duties and has not had fair access to markets. The news comes after Trump recently imposed steep tariffs on steel and aluminum from Canada, Mexico, and the European Union.

left.newsTitle: Trump brings chaos to G7 with trade threats and praise for Russia – and then backs out of joint agreement

Justice Samuel Alito wrote the majority opinion, noting right off the bat that an estimated one...

Instead, they were arguing that they had suffered harms because they were Democrats, and Democrats as a whole were underrepresented...

right.newsTitle: Trump Calls out Harley-Davidson for Moving Production Overseas Due to Tariffs
newBody: President Donald Trump called out Harley-Davidson for moving some of its production overseas due to tariffs placed on the U.S. by European countries.

center.newsTitle: EU tariffs force Harley-Davidson to shift some production overseas
newBody: Production of Harley-Davidson motorcycles sold in Europe will move from U.S. factories to facilities overseas, the Milwaukee-based company announced Monday, a consequence of the retaliatory tariffs the EU is imposing on American exports in an escalating trade war with the Trump administration.

issue: Harley Davidson to Move Production Overseas Due to Tariffs
roundup: Harley Davidson will move production of motorcycles sold in Europe from U.S. facilities to factories overseas in order to offset retaliatory EU tariffs on American exports.

left.newsTitle: Schumer on Waters: Calling for harassment 'not American'
newBody: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer sharply criticized fellow Democrat Rep. Maxine Waters of California on Monday for calling on opponents of President Donald Trump to protest his policies by harassing members of his administration.

right.newsTitle: Representative Andy Biggs: Maxine Waters Should Resign
newBody: Representative Andy Biggs (R-AZ) is calling for Representative Maxine Waters (D-CA) to resign after she urged supporters to harass Trump administration officials.

center.newsTitle: Congressional Leaders Criticize Maxine Waters For Urging Confrontation
newBody: A senior California Democratic lawmaker added some fresh fuel to the raging debate over civility in politics with a call for public confrontations with Trump administration officials.

issue: Congressional Leaders Criticize Maxine Waters
roundup: Congressional leaders criticize Maxine Waters for urging harassment of members of the Trump Administration.

left.newsTitle: Supreme Court rules in favor of Trump’s travel ban
newBody: The court says the ban is a typical government policy — not an expression of Trump’s feelings about Muslims.

right.newsTitle: Supremes Deal Victory For Trump, Uphold Travel Ban

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court upholds Trump travel ban
newBody: The Supreme Court in a 5-4 ruling on Tuesday upheld President Trump’s ban on nationals from five Muslim-majority countries from entering the United States.

issue: Supreme Court Upholds Trump Travel Ban
roundup: The Supreme Court upholds the Trump travel ban, saying that the ban is a typical government policy — not an expression of Trump’s feelings about Muslims.

left.newsTitle: U.S. Debt on Track to Grow to 'Highest Level in U.S. History by Far' Says CBO
newBody: America’s growing budget deficit will increase debt to the highest level in U.S. history by far, according to the Congressional Budget Office 2018 long-term budget outlook.

right.newsTitle: Federal debt to reach $100 trillion: CBO
newBody: The government is now staring at $100 trillion in total debt, the Congressional Budget Office said Tuesday, chronicling the disastrous trajectory of federal fiscal health.

center.newsTitle: CBO: Rising Interest Would Increasingly Pressure Government Finances
newBody: Rising interest rates will put increasing pressure on government finances and push interest payments to record levels in the coming decades, the Congressional Budget Office said Tuesday.

issue: Congressional Budget Office Says National Debt Headed Toward Historic Levels
roundup: The U.S. national debt is headed towards historic levels, expected to double to 152 percent of the economy by 2048, according to the Congressional Budget Office. Primary factors include the recent tax cuts, which the GOP is currently considering making permanent for individuals, as well as increasing costs of Social Security and Medicare.

left.newsTitle: Supreme Court’s anti-abortion ruling in California upholds the right to misinform
newBody: There’s a reason California lawmakers in 2015 required “crisis pregnancy” centers to disclose if they’re unlicensed, and to post signs telling patients the state provides free or cheap “prenatal care and abortion for eligible women.” It’s the same reason the centers exist at all.

right.newsTitle: Supreme Court NIFLA decision is major victory for pro-life groups and women, vindication for First Amendment
newBody: Tuesday’s 5-4 Supreme Court decision overturning a California law that required pro-life pregnancy centers to provide women with information about abortion is a victory for the First Amendment, for women seeking support during their pregnancies, and for the pregnancy centers.

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court rules against California law targeting anti-abortion pregnancy centers
newBody: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dealt a major blow to a California law requiring anti-abortion pregnancy centers to inform women about publicly funded abortion and contraception services.

issue: Supreme Court Overturns California Law Requiring Faith-Based Pregnancy Centers to Disclose Abortion Options
roundup: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a 5-4 decision overturning a California law that required faith-based crisis pregnancy centers to provide information about publicly funded abortion and contraception services. Supporters have celebrated the ruling as a victory for the pro-life movement and for free speech. Detractors have said it will spread misinformation about abortion, particularly since the pregnancy centers are not licensed medical clinics.

left.newsTitle: Supreme Court Rules 5-4 In Janus Union Fees Case
newBody: The conservative majority of the Supreme Court delivered a sweeping and historic blow to the labor movement Wednesday, ruling that public sector workers who are represented by unions cannot be required to pay any union dues.

right.newsTitle: Supreme Court rules against public sector unions, says employees can’t be forced to pay dues
newBody: The Supreme Court ruled  5-4 Wednesday in Janus v. AFSCME that public sector unions do not have a constitutional right to be able to force employees to pay dues. From now on, employees will have to give consent before any money from their paycheck goes to support a public-sector union. This ruling does not involve unions at private companies.

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court Deals Blow To Government Unions
newBody: In a blow to organized labor, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that government workers who choose not to join a union cannot be charged for the cost of collective bargaining.

issue: Supreme Court Rules Public Sector Unions Can't Force Members to Pay Dues
roundup: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday in Janus v. AFSCME that public sector unions do not have a constitutional right to force employees to pay union dues.

left.newsTitle: Justice Kennedy Retiring; Supreme Court to Become Trump Court
newBody: America is screwed, even more than it already was.

right.newsTitle: Possible Justice Kennedy retirement would give Trump opportunity to tilt Supreme Court to right
newBody: Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy might retire from the bench as early as this summer, a GOP senator said, and if true,  President Trump would be able to nominate a justice who could tilt the nation’s highest court well to the right for the foreseeable future.

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy Announces Retirement
newBody: Anthony M. Kennedy, one of the Supreme Court’s most consequential modern-day justices and author of landmark rulings on gay rights, the death penalty and campaign finance, announced his retirement Wednesday, handing President Donald Trump a historic opportunity to reshape the court.

issue: Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy Announces Retirement
roundup: Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy announced his retirement Wednesday. President Donald Trump now has the opportunity to nominate a replacement, which could reshape the court.

issue: Putin-Trump Summit Set for July 16 in Helsinki
roundup: Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump will hold a summit in Helsinki on July 16, the Kremlin and the White House announced Thursday.

issue: Shooting at Maryland Newspaper

newBody: President Trump on Saturday defended Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in the face of calls by some Democrats to abolish the agency, saying the agents are “doing a fantastic job” and that scrapping the agency “will never happen."

center.newsTitle: New York's Kirsten Gillibrand, Bill de Blasio echo progressive calls to 'abolish ICE'

issue: Several Democrats Call to Abolish ICE, President Trump Responds
roundup: In the wake of President Trump's "zero tolerance" immigration policy, several Democrats have called to abolish the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), with the president responding that it "will never happen."

left.newsTitle: Protests Across U.S. Call for End to Migrant Family Separations

While the occupant of the White House was away for the weekend at his Bedminster, N.J., golf club, images of the rallies were broadcast by cable news networks throughout the day.

right.newsTitle: Thousands turn out in cities across nation to protest separation of illegal immigrant families
newBody: Thousands of protesters marched in the streets of cities across America to protest the nation’s immigration policies and call for the reunification of parents and children who were separated at the U.S.-Mexico border, according to published reports.

center.newsTitle: Protesters across U.S. call on Trump to reunite immigrant families
newBody: Tens of thousands of protesters marched in cities across the United States on Saturday to demand the Trump administration reverse an immigration crackdown that has separated children from parents at the U.S-Mexico border and led to plans for military-run detention camps.

issue: Nationwide Protests Against Immigrant Family Separation
roundup: Thousands of protesters marched in cities across the United States on Saturday calling for an end to the separation of immigrant families at the border. These protests come after President Trump's June 20 executive order that says families will now be detained together.

left.newsTitle: Lopez Obrador scores landslide victory as Mexico votes for change

right.newsTitle: Mexico backs left-wing 'messiah' Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador in historic presidential election
newBody: In an election many Mexicans hope will be a turning point for a country beset by decades of corruption, violence and enduring poverty, voters turned to a left-wing populist some supporters refer to as a “messiah.” A savior from the two major parties that have failed to deliver on promises of reform, in the eyes of many voters.

center.newsTitle: Mexico elects Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador president by wide margin

issue: Left-Leaning Populist Andres Obrador Wins Mexico's Presidential Election

newBody: A federal judge in Washington, D.C. ruled Monday that the federal government must consider on a case-by-case basis whether asylum-seekers who have been detained represent a flight risk or credible danger to the public.

center.newsTitle: Judge rules that Trump administration has been wrongly detaining asylum seekers
newBody: A federal judge ruled on Monday that the Department of Homeland Security has violated its own policies by refusing to release most asylum-seekers from immigration detention even if they are likely to win their asylum case.

issue: Judge Rules Asylum Seekers Must Receive Individual Parole Hearings, Orders DHS to Stop Blanket Detentions
roundup: A federal judge ruled on Monday that the Department of Homeland Security has violated its own policy by issuing blanket detentions for asylum-seekers, ordering the department to decide each status in an individual parole hearing.

left.newsTitle: Judge: Students Have No Right to Literacy

right.newsTitle: Judge to Detroit Students: We Can’t Force Schools to Actually Teach You Anything
newBody: A federal judge has made it very clear in a new ruling that the government can force you to send your kids to school, but you can't force the government to actually provide an education there.

center.newsTitle: Michigan judge rules kids don't have a fundamental right to literacy
newBody: A Michigan judge ruled last week that children do not have a fundamental right to learn how to read and write.

issue: Judge Rules Students Do Not Have Fundamental Right to Literacy

left.newsTitle: Trump's Supreme Court pick to come down to personal chemistry and 'central casting image'
newBody: How will Donald Trump pick his new Supreme Court nominee? It’s Donald Trump, so the answer is obviously personal chemistry (no doubt with a heavy dose of how loyal he thinks they’ll be) plus optics. Trump is starting out with a pre-approved list of far-right judges and legal thinkers courtesy of the Federalist Society, so from there he can go with his gut, knowing that the right-wing legal and political establishments will nod along approvingly.

right.newsTitle: Another Justice Like Gorsuch, Please
newBody: "We have to STOP the next Trump nominee!" says a pop-up solicitation on People for the American Way's website. Before you rush to "donate now," you might want to consider the organization's assessment of Trump's last Supreme Court nominee.

center.newsTitle: Supreme Court nominee short list features candidates President Trump likes for different reasons
newBody: President Donald Trump says he likes all of his potential Supreme Court nominees.
Aides and advisers say he likes them for different reasons.

issue: Trump Narrows Candidates for Kennedy Replacement
roundup: President Trump announced today the top 3 candidates for filling Justice Kennedy's seat on the Supreme Court. It remains unclear at this time if he is leaning towards any of the 3 in particular, though they each have their own strengths and weaknesses.

center.newsTitle: White House Taps Former Fox News Executive For Senior Communications Job

issue: Former Fox News President Bill Shine Hired as White House Communications Director

right.newsTitle: Don't throw Scott Pruitt to the partisan wolves

center.newsTitle: Under fire for ethics scandals, EPA chief Pruitt resigns

center.newsTitle: Trump launches $34 billion trade war and China 'immediately' fires back

roundup: The economy added 213,000 jobs in June, up from the 190,000 expected. The unemployment rate rose from 3.8 percent to 4 percent, which analysts believe is a positive sign of increased labor force participation.

left.newsTitle: Secretary of State Pompeo leaves North Korea with promise of more talks but no tangible breakthrough

right.newsTitle: The other North Korea threat -- that almost never gets talked about

center.newsTitle: Pompeo says made progress with North Korea, more work needed

issue: Secretary of State Pompeo Meets with North Korea

center.newsTitle: Trump administration halts billions in insurance payments under Obamacare

issue: White House Suspends Billions in Obamacare Insurer Payments
